88## GPT in a tab
89
90
91Train a small transformer in your browser, on your GPU, with hand-written WebGPU kernels. Watch
92the moment it learns to copy. Then take it apart: knock out heads, patch activations between
93runs, and read its residual stream through a sparse autoencoder trained in WebGPU. No server, no
94model download, no machine-learning library; the model you dissect is the one you just trained.
95
96
97### Ten seconds with it
98
991. Open the page. Within 150 ms a recorded run of this same code is on the trace, dim, marked
100REF. Its blue copy loss falls off a cliff at step 1,500, labelled "recorded: L2·H4 learned to
101copy at step 1,500". Your own run starts training over it in under a second.
1022. Wait about 20–30 seconds. Your run reaches the same cliff, and the trace writes it in orange:
103L2·H4 learned to copy at step 1,500 · copy loss 4.06 → 0.97 nats. The head's lane under the
104trace turns orange, and its partner, a head that attends to the previous character, is outlined.
1053. When the run ends, open Heads. Shift-click the copying heads to knock them out. On random
106characters shown twice, the trained model continues the copy 40 of 40 characters right; without
107those two heads, 0 of 40.
1084. Open Features. Pick a feature and pin it at three times its strongest activation. Feature
109#918 fires on the "X" that starts the sonnets' Roman numerals; pinned, the model writes
110XXXXXXXX… and nothing else.
111
112### The techniques
113
114#### Induction heads, forming live
115
116Olsson et al. 2022, In-context Learning and Induction Heads.
117
118Every 20 training steps the GPU runs the standard test, between training steps and in the same
119command stream. It takes 32 rows of 64 random characters, each shown twice. For every head it
120measures the prefix-matching score: the attention each position of the second copy pays to
121the character just after the previous occurrence of its own character. It also measures the
122previous-character score, and the loss on each copy. A head counts as an induction head
123when its prefix-matching score reaches 0.3 and the second copy has become at least 1 nat easier
124than the first. The first reading where that happens is the moment. The trace marks it in
125words, draws the cliff in the copy loss (CH4) from the plateau, and lights the head's lane. The
126scoring is three small WGSL kernels (probe_attn, probe_loss, plus a pattern copy) appended to
127a forward pass. Their CPU reference is scoreProbe in src/model/probe.ts.
128
129What it took to see the moment within a minute. The finding first:
130- On text alone, no head learned to copy within the budget. That held for 3,000 steps on the
131sonnets and 3,000 on the five tragedies. A strong previous-character head formed on both, but
132no induction head. Olsson et al. see the phase change after hundreds of millions of tokens; a
133minute here is about 7 million.
134- So one training window in four is random characters: a run of 12 to 48 characters,
135repeated to fill the window. Nothing in it can be memorised, so the only way to predict a repeat
136is to copy it.
137- The period varies from window to window, so a head cannot pass by looking a fixed distance
138back. The test uses runs of 64, longer than any repeat the model trained on.
139
140The controls I ran, in this repository's tests/gpu/induction.html, with the probe on CPU
141snapshots:
142
143training data · induction head
144| --- | --- |
145text only (sonnets, tragedies), 3,000 steps · none
146one window in four a repeated passage of the text · none in 1,700 steps (the model memorises the text, so copying never pays)
147one in two: random characters with a fixed period of 64, no dropout, constant learning rate · at about step 2,850
148one in eight: random characters, varying period · none in 2,000 steps
149one in four: random characters, varying period (shipped) · step 1,100–1,600 across the seeds and dropout settings tried; 1,500 for the shipped seed
150
151Training is deterministic for a seed on a given GPU. The live run and the recorded one both found
152L2·H4 at step 1,500, with its partner L1·H2 attending to the previous character (score 0.99).
153
154#### Causality: knockouts and activation patching
155
156When the run ends, the GPU repeats the forward pass with a head_edit kernel spliced in before
157each layer's output projection. The kernel scales each head's output (0 knocks it out) and can
158add the same head's output saved from another run.
159
160- Knockout (zero-ablation): for each of the 16 heads, the change in loss on held-out text and
161on the test's second copy.
162- Activation patching (Meng et al. 2022, and as used by
163Olsson et al.):
164 - Clean run: the test.
165 - Corrupted run: the first copy replaced with other random characters, so the second copy
166has nothing to copy from.
167 - Patched runs: the corrupted run, once per head, with that head's output taken from the
168clean run, measuring how much of the copying returns.
169
170Results on the shipped run (step 2,250):
171
172head · its job (from the test) · knocked out: copy loss · knocked out: text loss · patched in: copying restored
173| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
174L1·H2 · previous character (1.00) · +4.65 nats · +0.84 · −5%
175L1·H1 · · +2.84 · +0.10 · −2%
176L2·H4 · induction (0.89) · +1.31 · −0.00 · 79%
177L2·H3 · induction (0.88) · +0.78 · +0.00 · 69%
178
179Read together: the induction heads carry the copy, and they depend on the previous-character head.
180Patching the previous-character head alone restores nothing, because the head that copies still
181reads the corrupted first copy.
182
183The page also lets you knock heads out while the model writes. Generation runs on the CPU in
184workers, through a key/value-cache decoder with the same hooks. One demonstration does it on
185random characters shown twice, continued greedily: **40 of 40 right as trained, 0 of 40 with
186L2·H3 and L2·H4 knocked out.**
187
188#### A sparse autoencoder, trained in WebGPU
189
190Bricken et al. 2023, Towards Monosemanticity;
191Cunningham et al. 2023, Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models.
192
193After the run, the trained model reads the whole training text in consecutive windows. The
194residual stream entering its last block is kept at every position: 86,016 vectors of 128.
195- Shape: an autoencoder with 1,024 features (8×) learns to rebuild those vectors:
196f = ReLU(x·W_enc + b_enc), x̂ = f·W_dec + b_dec.
197- Loss: squared error plus λ = 2 times the sum of activations. Inputs are scaled so the average
198vector has squared length 128.
199- Training: Adam, 3,000 steps of 4,096 vectors, with the decoder rows renormalised to unit
200length after every step. It takes about 9 seconds.
201
202Everything runs on the GPU:
203- the existing tiled matmul and AdamW kernels;
204- new kernels for the random row gather, the ReLU, the loss gradients, decoder normalisation and
205error sums;
206- a top-k kernel that scans every position for each feature's 12 strongest contexts and its
207firing count.
208
209Measured on the shipped run: 15.0% of the residual stream's variance unexplained; 14.7
210features active per character on average; 0.0% dead features (none that never fires). These are
211fidelity numbers, not a quality score. I did not measure the loss with the reconstruction spliced
212back into the model ("loss recovered").
213
214Labels are by rule, never by a model. Each candidate rule is a test on one context:
215- the character itself, or the one before or after it;
216- the word it is in, or the word just before it;
217- the start or end of a word or line, capitals, vowels, punctuation.
218
219A feature's label is the most specific rule, or pair of rules, that holds for at least 9 of its 12
220strongest contexts, with specificity discounted by coverage. It is shown with its count: "holds
221for 12 of the 12 strongest contexts". 675 of the 1,024 features get a label; the rest are shown
222as examples only. Typical labels: "“t” ending a word", "“u” after “r”", "the space after
223“and”", "“X” after a line break".
224
225Pinning a feature while the model writes: at the residual stream entering the last block, the
226decoder adds (value − f_j(x)) · d_j. That sets feature j to the chosen value and leaves
227everything the autoencoder does not explain untouched (clampFeature in src/cpu/sae.ts).
228
229### Live and recorded
230
231Recorded (npm run record, scripts/record.mjs):
232- The recording is this code's production build, run headless in Chromium with WebGPU, trained
233on the sonnets and dissected, on 2 Nov 2026 on this machine's GPU (Apple, Metal).
234- It ships as public/recorded/run.json (92 KB, 17 KB gzipped: trace, induction readings, the
235moment, knockouts, patching, autoencoder summary), features.json (218 KB, 75 KB gzipped,
236fetched when Features first opens) and weights.bin (2.1 MB of half-precision weights).
237Model weights stay out of the repository: weights.bin is not committed, and npm run record
238writes it. Without it, the page shows the download's failure state and everything else works.
239- It is the REF waveform on the trace from the first frame. In Heads and Features it is behind a
240Live/Recorded switch, and its weights are fetched only when you ask to write with it.
241- The download states its size first, shows progress, can be cancelled, is kept in the Cache API,
242and fails with a message while the rest of the page keeps working.
243
244Live: everything else. Your run, its moment, its knockouts and patching, its autoencoder,
245and everything you write with it.
246
247Without WebGPU (Firefox today, many phones):
248- A 62,016-parameter model (2 layers of 2 heads) trains live on the CPU in a worker, and the
249induction test runs on it every 20 steps.
250- In 3,000 steps (about three minutes) that small model formed no induction head; the page says
251so ("No induction head yet") rather than pretending.
252- The microscope shows the recorded GPU run, labelled. With its weights loaded, knockouts and
253pinned features write on the CPU.
254
255### Quickstart
256
257```sh
258npm install
259npm run dev # http://localhost:5173
260```
261
262A browser with WebGPU (current Chrome or Edge, Safari 26) trains the full model. ?cpu forces the
263fallback, ?text=alice|tragedies|words|kernels picks another text, and ?hold loads without
264starting. npm run build writes a static site to dist/.

353## Real or Hallucinated?
354
355
356Ask a small browser model the same factual question five times, watch its answers gather into inferred meanings, and inspect the probabilities behind every word and link. Make your own call on a claim; a checked primary source settles it. The original daily five-claim game remains a separate blind round, with exact fabrication marks and source passages highlighted in context. A static TypeScript experiment by Harry Freeman, with optional on-device inference and no accounts, keys, tracking or hosted model API.
357
358### Run locally
359
360Node.js 22.13+ and npm. No keys or environment variables are required.
361
362```sh
363npm ci
364npm run dev
365```
366
367Open http://127.0.0.1:5177. The development port is unchanged. Both servers bind to loopback only. The watcher excludes generated browser caches/screenshots/docs and polls application files every 300ms, so local test artifacts cannot flood its module graph.
368
369For the static production preview:
370
371```sh
372npm run build
373npm run preview
374```
375
376Open http://127.0.0.1:4184. The preview uses the isolated QA port; the development port remains 5177. Nothing has been published.
377
378
379### Inspect the technique in ten seconds
380
381Open the page. Recorded model run is visible immediately: five actual generated answers arrive, then move into meaning groups. Click an answer for its original token probabilities, or Inspect the links for both entailment directions. Change the threshold to recompute the grouping. No weights download until you choose Load models & run. Recorded timing is compressed; output text and probabilities are unchanged.
382
383The selected shared model files total 889.1 MB, plus the runtime shown on the page. To prepare local live inference, check at least 10 GiB is free, then run:
384
385```sh
386npm run models:fetch
387```
388
389Weights go only to ~/Personal/.models/, with immutable revisions, sizes, SHA-256 digests and licences in its manifest and README. The dev/preview middleware streams only allowlisted files from that directory. There is no second repository copy. A desktop WebGPU adapter is required for live generation; phones and unsupported adapters retain the complete interactive recording. Progress, cancel, cache removal and failed-download states keep that recording usable. No inference request leaves the browser.
390
391### Method and measured evaluation
392
393Discrete semantic entropy, adapted from Farquhar, Kossen, Kuhn and Gal, Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy, Nature (2024). Five independent answers are sampled from Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct. DeBERTa xsmall NLI tests each pair in both directions. Complete-link grouping requires every within-group pair to entail both ways at a fixed 0.60 threshold. Entropy is −Σ p log₂ p, using each group's empirical share of five answers. Our conservative grouping differs from the paper's representative-based implementation.
394
395Token confidence is the original untempered model softmax probability, captured before repetition penalty, temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling. The displayed answer summary is a geometric mean. Entropy measures disagreement, not truth: a model can confidently repeat a falsehood. The additional forced binary claim verdict uses (1 + mean(entailment − contradiction)) / 2 ≥ 0.50, separately from entropy. That authored support index is not a calibrated truth probability. The checked source remains authoritative.
396
397Transformers.js was chosen because it exposes causal-model logits and NLI in a browser worker. Generation uses WebGPU; NLI uses one WebAssembly thread. WebKit isolates NLI in a second CPU-only ONNX Runtime worker to make persisted cached reload reliable; Chromium uses one combined worker. The official browser-only SDK is vendored without native image dependencies; ONNX Runtime is pinned separately. See the engine API and reproduction details, SDK provenance, and model licences.
398
399The evaluation records all 70 verified questions in headless Chromium using the same browser engine, five answers per question, without source passages or reference answers in the generation prompt. Per-question checkpoints, model revisions, exact parameters, browser version, engine-source digests, answers, tokens and NLI distributions accompany data/detector-recording.json. All selected weight files are size- and SHA-256-verified before recording. Superseded runtime diagnostics are explicitly separated in docs/experiments/; they are not accepted evaluation results.
400
401Measured on all 70 questions · Result
402|---|---:|
403Binary claim verdict accuracy · 42/70 · 60%
404Claim-support AUROC · 0.6482
405Semantic-entropy AUROC for first-answer errors · 0.6335
406Token-confidence error baseline AUROC · 0.6740
407First answer gives the requested fact · 20/70 · 28.6%
408
409Semantic entropy did not beat token confidence on this set. These are small models and a small, related question set, not a general benchmark. Error labels are AI-assisted editorial checks of the requested fact against the stored source quote, bound to exact answer and quote hashes. They do not audit every extra assertion; one ambiguous answer is conservatively marked incorrect. No independent human review has been performed. The page publishes the same results and every recorded verdict.
410
411The daily proof reveal is still available in Daily game: on the 1 November edition, the fabricated phrase “includes water vapour” is redlined, a margin note corrects it, and NOAA's original passage highlights “after water vapor has been removed.” The exact proof marks are authored, source-checked annotations.
412
413### Play and persistence
414
415Buttons, left/right arrow keys, and deliberate horizontal swipes all answer. Vertical swipes scroll. Answers lock immediately; reload restores the current reveal. Native dialogs, visible focus, reduced motion, clipboard denial, storage failure, offline bundled play, missing/invalid content, slow loading, and JavaScript-disabled states are designed explicitly.
416
41714 editions / 70 claims span science, nature, space, energy, climate, history, and technology. There are 35 real and 35 fabricated claims overall, with one to four real claims per edition. Each edition has five distinct source pages and at least three topics. The collection repeats every 14 days and says so in the archive.
418
419Dates use Europe/London, including DST. The anchor is 19 October 2026. The archive lists fourteen recent dates and allows any available earlier date. Only completing today's edition adds to a local streak; archive play never backfills one. A round left open after midnight retains its answers and clearly stops calling its old date “Today”.
420
421Progress is validated and saved in this browser, with guarded reads/writes. Clearing site data clears it. Local scores are editable; this is not a competitive leaderboard. Shared text is ASCII and contains only the date, score, and correctness pattern, never claims or their true/false verdicts.
422
423V3 opens the Lie detector; Daily game retains the blind puzzle and its editor's proof reveal. The source passage is intentionally sealed before a decision, chemical formulas are typeset only for display, and desktop controls follow the claim directly. The earlier v2.1 evidence report remains a dated historical record.
424
425### Evidence pipeline
426
427All original claims, fabricated alterations, corrections, and explanations were AI-authored for this project. Every verdict is grounded in a fetched public primary source. Fabrications avoid living people, company conduct, health/medical advice, and elections; their cited pages directly contradict the altered detail. Missing search results are never treated as proof of falsity.
428
429data/puzzles.json stores source URLs, titles, publishers, evidence quote excerpts, original check dates and response hashes, surrounding source sentences, context-check dates, and exact proof spans. Runtime validation rejects a fabrication mark unless it occurs exactly once in its claim, or context whose highlighted text does not match the stored evidence quote. Source context is extracted from the main document text where a <main> element exists, with adjacent sentences retained.
430
431```sh
432npm run verify
433```
434
435The verifier fetches all 18 unique source pages with bounded concurrency, timeouts, HTML validation, response-size limits, and HTTPS host checks. All 70 supporting and contradicting quotes must match. It writes data/verification.json; only a fully successful run constructs and atomically replaces the context-enriched puzzle file. Failed or invented context cannot partly refresh dates. Original claim-check dates and hashes are retained. There is no cache fallback after a failed fetch.
436
437Source passages typeset an explicit allowlist of chemical formulas (CO₂, H₂O, CH₄, N₂O) for display only, including spaces introduced by flattened source markup. Stored quotes, context spans and verifier inputs remain unchanged; HTML escaping still follows formatting.
438
439Matching normalises entities, case, whitespace, and typographic punctuation while retaining the words and numbers. Quote presence and context extraction do not prove interpretation: proof notes remain editorial judgements. The game displays dated bundled checks, not live data, and makes no external background requests. Original links navigate to their publishers only when opened.
440
441### Checks and screenshots
442
443The current IBM Plex build was measured with three fresh contexts per engine, one browser at a time. Both routes at both requested sizes record zero total startup CLS, including controlled delayed-font and warm-reload checks. Detailed evidence and browser API limits are recorded in docs/TYPOGRAPHY.md. First meaningful paint is the initial detector after two native animation frames; the five-answer gather begins at about 1.3 seconds. The heaviest case is chosen by total recorded answer length.
444
445Browser · Median meaningful paint · Median frame · P95 frame
446|---|---:|---:|---:|
447Chromium 153 · 61.5 ms · 16.7 ms · 16.7 ms
448WebKit 26.6 · 65.0 ms · 17.0 ms · 18.0 ms
449Firefox 155 · 57.0 ms · 8.3 ms · 9.1 ms
450
451Opener JavaScript/data modules total 169,487 bytes gzipped. All optional JavaScript build chunks across both runtime profiles total 374,527 bytes gzipped; a browser loads its selected profile lazily. WASM is 26.86 MB raw / 6.68 MB gzipped for WebGPU, plus 14.26 MB raw / 3.68 MB gzipped for WebKit's CPU-only checker. The optional selected weights total 889.1 MB. These are asset gzip sizes, not a claim that Vite's loopback preview compresses HTTP traffic. Local timings and headless frame intervals are not network or physical-phone guarantees. See the raw measurements.
452
453```sh
454npm run check
455npm run audit
456npm run verify
457```
458
459check runs strict TypeScript, Biome, offline contract tests, hash-bound recording/metric validation, the static build, and the dependency-licence allowlist. Tests cover entropy, complete-link grouping, AUROC ties, seeded sampling against an independent oracle, tensor boundaries, download accounting, cache failure, schema rejection, exact proof spans, context offsets, immutable display typography, all-or-nothing source refreshes, London dates/DST, scoring, streaks, sharing and corrupt/blocked storage.
460
461With the production preview running on 4184:
462
463```sh
464mkdir -p .cache/tmp
465TMPDIR="$PWD/.cache/tmp" npm run test:browser
466TMPDIR="$PWD/.cache/tmp" npm run test:detector
467CRITIQUE_PASS=pass-1 TMPDIR="$PWD/.cache/tmp" npm run shots:v3
468CRITIQUE_PASS=pass-2 TMPDIR="$PWD/.cache/tmp" npm run shots:v3
469TMPDIR="$PWD/.cache/tmp" npm run test:perf:v3
470```
471
472The Mac harness uses Playwright through createRequire from the existing installation named in the brief, importing no project code or assets. On this shared Mac, the harness reuses matching installed Playwright binaries, avoiding duplicate copies. It falls back to this project's ignored .cache/browsers/ only when necessary. A disk guard blocks local browser launches below 10 GiB; every browser is silent and engines run sequentially. Coordinate the shared browser slot before any suite. To install those exact-version binaries from this project's pinned Playwright CLI:
473
474```sh
475PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.cache/browsers" npx --no-install playwright install webkit firefox
476```
477
478CI uses the pinned local Playwright dependency, installs all three engines, and gates on the browser suite as well as unit/type/lint/build/licence/audit checks. For another machine, install all three binaries and run with CI=1 PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.cache/browsers". No remote workflow has been dispatched.
479
480The browser suite exercises all 70 claims and reveals in Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox, including 320px layouts, keyboard paths, reloads, streaks, archive dialogs, source-context highlighting, exact corrections, sharing, synthetic swipes, storage denial, and midnight rollover. The Date-only test clock preserves native Performance and animation timing.
481
482- shots/v3/pass-1/ and pass-2/: detector, inspectors, long/empty/error/loading/offline states, real live generation/cancel/cache states, paired screenshots and combined contact sheets.
483- shots/v3/daily/: both complete daily-game state passes.
484- shots/v3/detector-browser-report.json: the detector's serial three-engine functional checks.
485- shots/v3/browser-report.json: the daily game's serial three-engine functional/layout checks.
486- shots/v3/performance-report.json: three fresh runs per engine, actual frame intervals and gzipped asset sizes.
487- docs/V3-EVIDENCE.md and docs/V3-CRITIQUE.md: final results, method, two visual critiques and limits.
488- shots/v3/before/ and shots/v2/: earlier states, retained as historical evidence.
489- public/og.png: 1200×630 capture of the real running interface, not an illustration.
490
491IDENTITY.md records the newsroom direction: IBM Plex Sans for reading and interface text, Plex Mono for data/code/records, and Plex Sans Condensed for the wordmark, headings and labels. The white and near-black surfaces, red corrections, green source highlights and meaning-group motion remain. Eight Latin WOFF2 faces from @fontsource 5.3.0 are self-hosted with font-display: swap; the two main reading/wordmark faces are preloaded on cold navigation. No runtime font request goes to Google or another origin.
492
493### Credits and licences
494
495Original code, prose, and artwork: Copyright (c) 2026 Harry Freeman, MIT (LICENSE). Attributed source excerpts retain their publishers' material and reuse terms; they are not relicensed by the code licence. No agency logos or third-party photographs are bundled. Self-hosted IBM Plex fonts retain their SIL Open Font License 1.1 notices beside the files in public/fonts/. No endorsement is implied.
496
497Primary sources: NASA Science, NOAA National Ocean Service, NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, US Energy Information Administration, US National Park Service, and NIST.
498
499Reuse guidance checked: NASA, NOAA NOS, EIA, NPS, and NIST. The app uses attributed educational text excerpts under those policies, with no agency branding or third-party media. NOAA's climate page credits underlying research; the game quotes the agency's explanatory prose, not the referenced paper.
500
501ONNX Runtime is MIT; the vendored Transformers.js browser SDK and both selected models are Apache-2.0. npm dependencies are exactly pinned with one lockfile and checked against the MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / ISC allowlist. The generated inventory includes optional platform packages. Playwright is Apache-2.0. Harry separately approved OFL-1.1 for the self-hosted Plex fonts; their versions, source URLs, byte sizes, SHA-256 digests and original notices are checked by npm run licenses. See docs/dependency-licenses.json and docs/font-licenses.json.
502
503### Limits
504
505Fourteen editions repeat. Source interpretation and exact-span corrections are editorial. Tiny-model answers can be confidently false, repetitive or capped at 32 tokens; entropy depends on a fallible NLI model and five samples. The detector is an additional model inference, never a replacement for source proof. Checks are dated snapshots, not continuous monitoring. A full 70-question live eval was recorded in Chromium; WebKit live lifecycle checks cover the demo question, not a second 70-question benchmark. Phones and Firefox use the recorded experience; narrow live screenshots resize a desktop session and do not claim physical-phone inference. Physical-device swipes, a full assistive-technology audit, and independent human editorial acceptance remain unperformed. Local commits require explicit authorization; no pushes, accounts or publishing.

sections.title: Agent Race
sections.html:
508## Agent Race
509
510
511Two coding agents get the same bug, in fresh isolated repositories, on one clock. Agent Race records their real headless CLI streams and exposes their commands, edits and verification claims as a motorsport timing screen and an evidence flight recorder. The finish is independent hidden acceptance, with receipts checking recognized verification claims against command evidence and code fingerprints. The default recording is a fair, completed cache race: both agents ran their tests and passed all five hidden cases. This is a personal local experiment, not a model leaderboard.
512
513### Try it
514
515Node 22.12 or later and npm. No account, key, agent CLI or receipts checkout is needed to watch the bundled replay.
516
517```sh
518npm ci --ignore-scripts
519npm run build
520npm run preview
521```
522
523Open http://127.0.0.1:4317. The server binds to loopback and refuses to silently change ports. npm run dev starts the development server on the same address. The viewer invokes no models and has no upload, telemetry or backend. Replay data and the condensed display font are bundled locally. The viewer makes no external requests.
524
525The Flight recorder opens immediately, with a changed line connected back to its captured source read. Choose any +/− line in the final diff, or any node/edge in the time graph, to inspect its inferred evidence. The Recording selector includes both earlier failed races; the fair cache race remains the default. All inference is computed live in your browser from the original scrubbed JSON.
526
527Choose Race replay (or open /?view=replay) for the original broadcast. It starts at 8×, completing in about ten seconds; reduced motion starts paused. Scrub the shared timeline, choose a speed, or jump to Finish. Sector splits show first read, first edit, first test command and independent verification. The gap compares matching observed sectors. Click a command, change, claim or commentary source to inspect its evidence in an inline picture-in-picture panel. Space plays/pauses outside controls; left/right move five seconds. The range supports native keys including End. Escape closes inline evidence or dialogs and restores focus.
528
529Earlier attempts keeps the two original failed recordings downloadable and discloses the additional candidate rejected by the privacy scrub. The failed attempt was not rewritten to force a save.
530
531### Flight recorder: the technique
532
533The core is an evidence-labelled lexical provenance DAG and backward slice, inspired by Mark Weiser, Program Slicing, ICSE 1981. Start at a changed line; find earlier captured outputs containing the same code identifiers or complete changed lines; walk the inferred graph backwards. Common syntax, comments and string literals do not become identifier evidence. A failed command's actual output can supply evidence, but proposed code in its title cannot. No edge crosses agents or comes from the future. This borrows criterion-driven graph traversal, not semantic/dynamic program slicing or access to an agent's private reasoning.
534
535Every edge exposes its rule and text. File-to-test links are inferred associations. Claude's claim is mapped to the nearest earlier successful verify command, with the absent historical event-to-receipt ID association disclosed. Codex's unmatched wording remains without a receipt verdict. Final diffs are reconstructed by applying the captured transactions to the authored challenge baseline, with line ownership retained across edits; mismatched patches fail closed.
536
537Measured coverage: 51 of 124 changed lines (41.1%) have an earlier lexical match in the fair recording; the other 73 remain unlinked. There are 17 observed call/claim nodes and 16 inferred edges. An explicit 16/16 edge audit checks observable overlap/routing, not causal ground truth. Causal accuracy is unknown. Lexical overlap can be coincidental, and a missing match does not establish invention. No model is running, no weights download and no hosted inference occurs.
538
539### Signatures and the one-byte demo
540
541Choose Verify the recording +, then Change one byte. The browser changes a recorded exit from 0 to 1 in an in-memory payload, retaining valid JSON and the original signature. Native WebCrypto Ed25519 rejects it. Restore original verifies again. The byte window shows the actual payload, UTF-8 byte counts and domain-separated message.
542
543Two real imports, one per agent, were signed by the local receipts CLI retrospectively during this build. They use an in-toto Statement v1 inside DSSE v1, with Ed25519 signatures. The exact original payload bytes are verified before fatal UTF-8 decoding and schema validation. The browser pins a separately bundled raw public key, checks its SHA-256 fingerprint, then checks recording and import-file digests and association to the recorded event. DSSE key IDs are hints, not authenticated identities. Standard/URL-safe base64 are supported.
544
545The UI says exactly “signed at import from the recorded ledger”. Original execution argv, absolute cwd, shell flags, start/end times and separate stdout/stderr hashes/byte counts were not saved. All nine fields are literal null, with checked missingFields; stream-arrival observation metadata is separate. No missing evidence was reconstructed and no command was rerun. Subject digests describe signing-time bytes. The entire immutable recording, including its claims and failures, is bound by each signed subject digest; signing does not expand the original receipts claim grammar or establish test completeness.
546
547The key is project-local under ignored .receipts/keys/, with directory mode 0700 and private-key mode 0600. No home configuration is touched. The published public key is public/attestations/trusted-public.pem; the browser anchor is web/trusted-key.json. Fingerprint: 0d63ae2ec3299b5b5a47aad4c929bfe27b7989e4c78156067f3bb7efc990b461. This is the project's local trust anchor, not independent execution-time attestation or a third-party identity certificate. A compromised host could replace the viewer and key together.
548
549Verify an existing import with the local CLI (no signing or command execution):
550
551```sh
552node "$HOME/Personal/oss/receipts/dist/cli.js" verify \
553 public/attestations/codex-5.dsse.json \
554 --key public/attestations/trusted-public.pem --subject-root "$PWD" --json
555```
556
557node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/attest-recording.ts is the original import adapter. It checks the immutable recording hash, preserves only recorded facts, calls the sibling CLI and verifies its result before exporting public artifacts. Outputs are no-clobber: rerunning against the existing signed files fails intentionally. Viewing or checking does not need that script or a private key. Earlier failed recordings have no signed imports and display an explicit unavailable state. Unsupported WebCrypto also leaves the trace usable without a substitute verification result.
558
559### The default race
560
561The double fetch (single-flight), recorded 1 November 2026 at 12:50:14.922 UTC, with Claude Code 2.1.286 and Codex CLI 0.160.1. Both agents received the same multiline prompt and fresh copies of the same repo.
562
563Agent · Process exit · Visible test through receipts · Agent regression suite · Independent hidden tests · Verified finish
564| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
565Claude Code · 0 · 1/1 pass · 5/5 pass · 5/5 pass · 41.466 s
566Codex · 0 · 1/1 pass · 4/4 pass · 5/5 pass · 77.793 s
567
568Claude reached independent acceptance first, by 36.327 seconds. Timings include CLI startup, provider latency, work, process shutdown, claim checking and hidden execution. Codex's final message arrived before its process exited; the replay retains that gap. These are launch-to-acceptance measurements, not pure inference times or a general performance ranking.
569
570Claude encountered a blocked shell heredoc, saw that it had truncated its files, rewrote them through the Write tool and reran its tests. That failure and recovery stay visible. Both agents could run commands and the receipts-wrapped test suite in their own repo. The same filesystem boundaries applied to both lanes.
571
572The recording contains 20 observed normalized events, including five edit events. Save scrub: 36 known path references redacted, zero remaining findings. Two recognized final Claude claims are VERIFIED. Codex's final “Verification passed” wording does not match the current receipts grammar and remains an unannotated message; its command exits and independent acceptance are recorded separately.
573
574Original JSON: public/recordings/single-flight-2026-11-01T12-50-14-922Z.json. demo.json is its identical default replay copy. Scrubbed raw streams are retained in tests/fixtures/.
575
576### Record locally
577
578The harness requires macOS, sandbox-exec, Git, existing authenticated claude and codex CLIs, and a built local receipts checkout. It never signs in, creates accounts, fetches keys or changes global agent settings.
579
580```sh
581./bin/agent-race list
582./bin/agent-race smoke
583./bin/agent-race run single-flight
584```
585
586Receipts defaults to $HOME/Personal/oss/receipts/dist/cli.js. Set RECEIPTS_PATH to a different built repository root if needed; an empty optional value uses the default. The sibling is used read-only and is never copied or modified.
587
588The original two-attempt cap was explicitly extended by two attempts. All four authorised race attempts have now been used. Further run calls are blocked; the counter is not reset. Capability smoke jobs are separate, small read/command checks, not races or demo data. Offline tests and viewing remain available without further model use.
589
590Before reserving a race attempt, the harness requires a successful smoke report for both agents from the last 24 hours. It proves a file was read, an actual command created the expected nonce-bound output, the process exited zero and receipts VERIFIED the wrapped npm test. A failed, incomplete, duplicated-agent or expired proof blocks the race. Smoke has a 120-second per-agent bound and a $0.25 Claude CLI budget; races have 240 seconds per lane and a $2 Claude CLI budget. These are CLI controls, not billing guarantees. Neither tests nor CI invoke model-backed smoke automatically.
591
592#### Challenges
593
594Challenge · Weak visible test · Hidden acceptance
595| --- | --- | --- |
596single-flight — The double fetch · Sequential cache reuse · 5 cases: concurrent misses, rejection eviction, synchronous throw/retry, independent keys, undefined values
597unicode-slug — Lost in translation · ASCII “Hello World” · 9 cases: canonical equivalence, NFKD compatibility, combining marks, non-Latin text, separators, empty input
598date-window — One day too many · Checks only the first day · 8 cases: exclusive end, equal/reversed bounds, leap/year boundaries, strict dates, UTC changes
599
600Toy repos have no dependencies and use Node's built-in test runner. Hidden suites are visible in this source tree but are copied into a lane only after that agent exits. “Hidden” is a per-race filesystem boundary. Reference solutions are offline test fixtures and never replay events.
601
602### Harness and sandbox fixes
603
604The installed CLI help was checked. Both tools use their documented noninteractive interfaces inside an external macOS Seatbelt sandbox. Native approval bypass is used only because that external policy remains mandatory; Claude's nested tool sandbox is explicitly disabled to avoid conflicting wrappers.
605
606- Codex pre-event SIGKILL: the full multiline race prompt passed as argv through sandbox-exec reproducibly exited with SIGKILL before stdout/stderr, even with a failing localhost-only provider. Sending the exact same prompt through the documented codex exec --json … - stdin interface started normally and reached that provider. Production now keeps argv and stdin together in one launch plan, writes the prompt to the pipe and closes it. The launch contract test checks byte-identical prompt content for both agents. This is an observed input-transport failure, not an invented explanation about an update or login prompt.
607- Nested state canonicalization: Codex's stderr identified denied canonicalization of CODEX_HOME. The policy now permits metadata for the exact ancestor directories of each lane; sibling directory contents remain denied.
608- Claude command temp area: TMPDIR alone did not control its Bash working area. CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR is set to its lane's private root. Actual live smoke and the fair race verify command execution.
609- Node loading receipts: Node's realpath traversal failed at lstat '/Users' before the test runner could start. Exact ancestor metadata for the allowed receipts executable is permitted, while unrelated home contents stay denied.
610- Git warning / scrub failure: Git tried an implicit global ignore path in the real home and emitted a home-path warning. Lane-local XDG config/cache/state and explicit Git config isolation remove that warning. The privacy checker remains fail-closed.
611
612Each challenge repo is under /private/tmp/agent-race-…/<agent>/repo, with private CLI temp/state areas in that lane. The policy denies unrelated home contents, sibling temp trees, writes outside the lane and writes to .git after initialization. Narrow read exceptions serve the built receipts code and existing provider credential locations; the harness never opens credential contents. Auth belongs to the CLIs. Codex uses a clean HOME/CODEX_HOME and ignores user config/rules; Claude runs in safe mode without customisations or MCP. The prompt forbids private data, outside repos, network tools, dependencies, subagents, commits, pushes and publishing.
613
614The offline boundary check uses the actual nested layout and runs Node → receipts → npm → a test command inside it. It verifies both the receipt and positive read/write access, alongside home/sibling denial and Git-write denial. Successful process stderr and exit signals are retained for future diagnosis.
615
616A repeatable zero-model diagnostic is available with node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/diagnose-startup.ts. It points the CLI only at a deliberately failing loopback provider and keeps diagnostic output separate from race recordings.
617
618### Receipts and claims
619
620./verify wraps npm test with receipts. The checker binds a command's result to before/after/current code fingerprints. Each recognized claim is checked at its message boundary and final claims are checked again before hidden acceptance, so hidden tests cannot retroactively back an agent's words.
621
622The viewer supports VERIFIED, STALE, FAILED and UNBACKED. Receipts' MISMATCH/VAGUE statuses map to UNBACKED while preserving the original status and reason. Its grammar is bounded: unsupported wording can remain an ordinary message; absence of a badge is not verification. Numeric Node test summaries are not automatically evidence for every numeric phrase. The real integration test proves UNBACKED → VERIFIED → STALE → FAILED. A receipt proves the recorded command/fingerprint, not full test quality or completeness.
623
624Streams are timestamped from one monotonic clock, incrementally decoded across UTF-8 chunks, validated and normalized. Working-tree snapshots supply expandable unified diffs. Unknown envelopes remain in raw fixtures but create no invented action; malformed recognized events fail closed. Time/output/snapshot limits are enforced. Protected tests, package files and the verify wrapper are checked; source symlinks are rejected. Hidden acceptance runs inside the lane sandbox. Both lanes settle before normal/error cleanup.
625
626Before any recording save, only explicitly known roots are replaced with <repo>, <sandbox> and <receipts>. The entire candidate and raw event streams are checked for company names, emails, home paths and recognizable secret formats, including JSON-escaped forms. Any remaining finding blocks saving. The detector is conservative, not a proof that arbitrary encoded secrets are impossible. No agent events are fabricated or hand-edited.
627
628### Failed attempts remain disclosed
629
630- Attempt 1: both lanes failed before useful coding. Original recording retained; 25 path references redacted, zero findings.
631- Attempt 2: Codex died before events; Claude's edit passed 9 hidden Unicode cases but its commands were blocked. Original recording retained; 29 references redacted, zero findings.
632- Attempt 3 (first additional attempt): Codex still died with the multiline argv transport; Claude passed cache acceptance at the displayed 42.25 s. The scrub rejected a remaining home path. The full candidate was not saved. Terminal-only rejection report; no replay was reconstructed from it.
633- Attempt 4: the default fair race above. Both agents exit zero and pass all five hidden cases; 36 references redacted and zero findings.
634
635The failed pre-fix capability smoke is also preserved separately in shots/. Those jobs are labelled smoke, not a race. The final successful report is shots/agent-smoke.json.
636
637### Checks and visual QA
638
639V3 evidence, both critique passes, browser reports and limits are in docs/v3-verification.md, with screenshots under shots/v3/. node scripts/screenshots-v3.mjs exercises trace/proof states; node scripts/proof-fallbacks-v3.mjs tests unavailable verification and historical recordings. All browser launchers share scripts/silent.mjs: no live AudioContext, media playback or device access. Suites run one engine at a time, one worker.
640
641```sh
642npm run gate
643```
644
645This runs strict TypeScript (including diagnostic/build scripts), Biome, tests, the zero-model sandbox/toolchain check, production build, dependency licence checks and npm audit. The local receipts build is required for its integration test. Core tests cover normalization from captured streams, schemas, scrub rejection/escaping, timeline ordering, CLI input transport, readiness/budget guards, subprocess limits and all challenge acceptance contracts against bugs/reference fixes.
646
647The PR workflow targets a self-hosted macOS runner labelled agent-race, with Node and the built receipts sibling available (RECEIPTS_PATH may be a repository variable). No runner was provisioned and no hosted workflow was dispatched. CI configuration is distinct from local passing checks.
648
649With the production preview running, the v2 browser matrix is:
650
651```sh
652RACE_SHOT_PASS=pass5 RACE_BROWSERS=chromium,webkit,firefox node scripts/screenshots-v2.mjs
653```
654
655It uses the Playwright runtime explicitly approved by the brief. WebKit and Firefox binaries live under .race/browsers (installed using that runtime’s cli.js install webkit firefox with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.race/browsers"). No code from the runtime’s host project is read. The matrix captures 24 states at 1440×900 and 390×844 in each engine, including delays, missing/invalid/empty data, failed commands, both finish boundaries, inline patches, claims, long messages, keyboard focus and archive failures. Network interception supplies test-only boundary states; the shipped default always uses the original real recording.
656
657The matrix also measures meaningful paint and animation frame intervals. node scripts/contact-sheets.mjs pass5 makes inspection sheets. The two critique passes, browser observations and performance details are in v2 verification and shots/v2/. node scripts/social-preview.mjs creates the 1200×630 social image from the real rendered replay. IDENTITY.md records the visual decisions. The v2.1 typography verification records the self-hosted face, current screenshots and cold-load observations.
658
659### Deterministic race control
660
661src/core/broadcast.ts derives the booth commentary from immutable events. Every line names its rule and opens its exact source event. No model runs in the viewer. The shell recogniser handles the archive’s documented cat, ./verify, npm test and node --test command forms, preserving quoted strings and excluding heredoc bodies; it is deliberately not an arbitrary shell interpreter. Unsupported forms do not earn a sector split. A failed inner test overrides an outer shell exit of zero. A zero exit alone is never a passing test verdict.
662
663Edit commentary invalidates the inference from earlier tests; claim commentary reports the stored receipts verdict; independent acceptance alone supplies the finish. Unknown verification wording is disclosed explicitly. The finish graphic appears at the verified timestamp and occupies an existing event window, so the clock and commentary stay in place. The phrase “photo finish” describes this freeze-frame treatment, not a claim that a 36-second result was close.
664
665### Credits and licences
666
667Created by Harry Freeman. MIT: Copyright (c) 2026 Harry Freeman.
668
669- receipts — Harry Freeman's local MIT evidence checker, called through its CLI.
670- Zod — MIT. diff — BSD-3-Clause. TypeScript — Apache-2.0.
671- Vite, Vitest, tsx — MIT. Biome — MIT OR Apache-2.0.
672- All 130 locked npm packages, including optional platform binaries, satisfy MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / ISC. Full inventory.
673- IBM Plex Sans (400, 400 italic, 500, 600), IBM Plex Mono (400, 600), IBM Plex Sans Condensed (500, 600) — eight unmodified Latin WOFF2 files from @fontsource 5.3.0, self-hosted under SIL OFL-1.1, 165,476 bytes total. Sans reads, Mono records, Condensed signs. Full OFL notices sit beside them. Pinned sources, sizes and hashes; npm run licenses checks the manifest. Three main faces are preloaded and all faces use font-display: swap. No external runtime font request. Plex reset verification records before/after layout shift and screenshots.
674
675No employer code, client data, private transcripts or prior user session recordings are included. No accounts or logins were used. Harry authorised a local commit on main on 3 November 2026; no remote, push or publishing is authorised. A project-local Git root was initialized only because receipts requires one for key isolation. Original challenge prompts, agent messages and diffs remain as observed after path scrubbing.
676
677### Remaining limits
678

Shell heredocs can still hit the stricter temporary-file boundary; that recovery is preserved in the match. The four-race allowance is exhausted. The v2 brief conditionally permits one extra race only after a material harness change; this viewer-only revision uses none. There are no remaining blockers to viewing the fair race locally.

682## Grid Weather
683
684
685Great Britain's wind, sun and electricity carbon, on one forecast chart. A real ECMWF 100 m wind field drives 131,072 GPU tracers on desktop and 32,768 on phones. Under the map, a ten-feature ridge forecaster trains in a browser worker, draws its next 48 hours against NESO, and exposes its held-out errors and feature contributions. Inputs and recorded calculations carry their dates. No hosted model, key, account or downloaded model weights.
686
687### Run
688
689Node.js 24 or later:
690
691```sh
692npm ci --ignore-scripts
693npm run dev
694```
695
696Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. The server binds to loopback. The port is unchanged. npm run build creates the static app; npm start serves it. No environment variables are needed.
697
698### See it in ten seconds
699
700The opening wind replay is a recorded integration from this code and the genuine dated field. It is embedded in the page so there is something to see before the weather JSON arrives. The live WebGL2 solver replaces it after priming one second of real advection and completing its first GPU frame. Wind / Sun / Carbon changes the underlay. On a phone, use Layer beside the time controls. Present forecast tours carbon changes together with sourced wind and sunlight stories; every caption prints its evidence.
701
702Model opens the forecaster. A recorded calculation is labelled while the same ridge code trains locally. Held-out replay compares the model, the frozen NESO forecast and the later target at the same times. The hypothetical wind slider changes only the model's forward input; it is not a causal intervention and never changes the NESO line or the measured backtest score.
703
704The regional outlook, cleanest two-hour windows, table, keyboard map, source dialogs, reduced motion and explicit dated offline states remain. Opening a dialog pauses the carbon tour. Wind is weather, never electricity or carbon flowing between regions.
705
706### The physical field
707
708Public Open-Meteo ECMWF data: wind speed/direction at 100 m above ground, total cloud cover, surface shortwave radiation and 2 m temperature. The explicitly selected model is ECMWF IFS 0.25°. Open-Meteo interpolates its native time steps to hourly values; shortwave radiation is the preceding-hour mean.
709
710We sample a 100 km British National Grid lattice, 18×16 points over GB and adjacent seas. An inverse Airy transverse-Mercator projection and a seven-parameter Helmert transform locate those points in WGS84. This is a weather sampling approximation, not an OSTN15 surveying conversion. Wind vectors are rotated into grid east/north. The renderer bilinearly samples the vector field and linearly interpolates between source hours; it never extrapolates past the field's coverage.
711
712Regional means use 10 km equal-area quadrature cells inside the actual DNO polygons, including polygon holes. London has eight such cells in this geometry; cell counts are recorded. We average wind-speed magnitudes, rather than taking the magnitude of an average vector. These are land-area proxies, not turbine-capacity weights, and omit offshore farms outside the DNO areas. The correlation table reports Pearson r and actual paired n, including undefined correlations for constant series. Hourly samples are autocorrelated; n is not a count of independent observations and no significance claim is made.
713
714src/wind-gpu.ts keeps positions/ages/seeds in two transform-feedback buffers. A second-order explicit midpoint step advances every particle using the real velocity field. Two RGBA framebuffers retain and fade trails. Particle colour follows speed, and motion is 1,200× real time. These are virtual tracers in the field selected by the timeline, not observed air-parcel tracks. Source changes clear old trails; opacity tapers inside the sampling boundary. All particle states are simulated; the phone uses a smaller explicit budget. A worker owns the graphics context and bounds work to one frame in flight.
715
716The reference CPU midpoint integrator generates public/wind-recorded.svg from the same source field and units. Its 477 paths and 189 playback tracers are explicitly recorded. Live GPU positions are computed afresh, not played back. If WebGL2, OffscreenCanvas or the graphics worker is unavailable, source-derived wind vectors and sunlight cells remain. Reduced motion uses those static fields.
717
718### The forecaster and its score
719
720Ridge regression — Hoerl & Kennard (1970) is a good fit for a short, correlated time series: it is small, stable and inspectable, and needs no pretrained download. We implement the standardized normal equations with Cholesky factorization. The intercept is unpenalized. Lambda is selected from 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 on an earlier chronological validation slice, using scaling learned only on that slice's training rows. The final fit uses all permitted training rows.
721
722Features: wind speed, capped speed cubed, cloud, shortwave radiation, temperature, two daily Fourier harmonics (four terms) and intensity 24 hours earlier. Forecasts beyond 24 hours consume their own earlier predictions. Missing recent GB actuals are bridged with model warm-up predictions, not future targets. Intensity outputs are bounded to 0–2,000 gCO₂/kWh; the equation/contribution view discloses this bound. Contributions are associations, not causal effects.
723
724The comparator is the regional API's GB aggregate (id 18); the GB target is the separate national actual series. The comparison freezes the genuine NESO forecast captured 1 November 2026, 16:02 UTC (public/backtest-neso.json). Training ends two hours before that issue time. No held-out target enters scaling, tuning or recursive predictions. The as-issued weather archive was unavailable during preparation, so the retrospective test uses an explicitly labelled 48-hour seasonal-persistence weather forecast. The forward prediction uses the actual weather forecast in the input capture. Historical training-data vintages were not preserved; this is not a fully operationally vintaged evaluation.
725
726The bundled GB result, against NESO's national actual intensity series, is 49.4 gCO₂/kWh MAE for ridge versus 31.8 for the frozen NESO forecast and 42.6 for daily persistence, over 21 paired hours. NESO wins, and the simple persistence baseline also beats this model. Regional targets are NESO's historical estimates: their scores measure revisions, not independently observed emissions. All per-region scores and counts are shown, not just the best result. A short window does not establish general forecast skill.
727
728src/forecaster.ts is used unchanged by the browser worker and by scripts/record-model.mjs. The recorded output includes the core source SHA-256 and its source date. Tests recompute all 15 results, all 48-hour series and the score inputs. No coefficients are downloaded to impersonate training; the browser actually fits the models. Recorded inputs and recorded outputs remain separately labelled from live computation.
729
730Additional technique reference: WebGL 2 transform feedback specification.
731
732### Sources, cache and refresh
733
734Electricity: the public NESO Carbon Intensity API, regional current/history/forecast plus the national actual series. Every response crosses a runtime validator. Regional historical values are estimates; only the explicitly named national target uses the API's actual series. The GB aggregate is never invented by averaging regional intensities.
735
736Refresh weather fetches 288 public sample points in small sequential batches: approximately 2.4 MB of JSON for the current request shape. Progress and Cancel are visible. Successful responses are validated and cached in the browser for 30 minutes; failed/cancelled downloads retain the dated snapshot. Refreshed weather and model-training inputs have separate provenance labels. The carbon API cache remains 15 minutes. Normal builds fetch nothing.
737
738To deliberately prepare new recorded inputs:
739
740```sh
741npm run refresh:v3
742npm run build
743```
744
745The source manifest, URLs, byte counts and capture times are data/v3-sources.json. Raw preparation responses stay in .cache/v3-data/. A failed preparation does not update the served build. Disk headroom is checked before preparation. The frozen November 1 NESO comparison remains frozen; it is never silently replaced by today's forecast. public/model-recording.json is a calculation from our own code and public data, not a hosted-model response.
746
747### Checks and visual review
748
749```sh
750npm run check
751npm run test:browser
752```
753
754The local gate checks strict TypeScript, safety/syntax lint, data/model/geometry/projection/advection tests, the build and package licences. Browser automation is silent: Chromium is muted, Firefox volume is zero, and all engines use the V3 device-free AudioContext pattern. On macOS, accelerated Chromium tests explicitly use ANGLE Metal (the default headless backend otherwise chose SwiftShader). Browser suites must run one engine at a time, with no overlapping suite. The brief-authorized existing Playwright SDK is the only external test tool used. Temporary profiles and downloads remain inside the project cache. Do not start a suite while another builder holds the browser slot. The harness checks for 10 GiB free plus profile headroom before every launch and reuses exact global test-browser builds when available.
755
756Final browser results, native timings, both critique passes and screenshots are recorded in shots/v3/ and QA.md. Node benchmark time is not reported as browser training time. Browser meaningful paint, GPU readiness, animation frame intervals and completed worker GPU-frame latency are measured separately. No remote CI workflow, commit or deployment is implied by a local pass.
757
758### Credits and licences
759
760- Original code: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Harry Freeman.
761- Electricity: National Grid ESO / NESO Carbon Intensity API, CC BY 4.0.
762- Weather: Open-Meteo / ECMWF, CC BY 4.0. Modified by projection, rotation, interpolation and area averaging. Open-Meteo's free endpoint is non-commercial, with fair-use limits: fewer than 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour and 600/minute. This is a local personal preview. No Open-Meteo server code is imported; its AGPL code is not a product dependency.
763- Boundaries: NESO DNO licence areas, NESO Open Data Licence. Supported by National Energy SO Open Data. Simplified and indicative, not a connection lookup.
764- TypeScript 5.9.3: development-only, Apache-2.0. Zero runtime packages, zero pretrained-weight downloads. No shared model-weight file is needed. DEPENDENCIES.md records tools and data.
765
766Local only. No private data, accounts, commits, pushes or publishing.
767
768
769### Typeface
770
771IBM Plex Sans is the reading/interface face, Mono carries numerical data and code, and Sans Condensed signs the broadcast. Eight latin WOFF2 faces from @fontsource5.3.0 are served locally with font-display:swap; the three main faces are preloaded. There are no runtime Google Fonts requests. Original per-family SIL OFL1.1 licences and a URL/size/SHA-256 manifest are in public/fonts/. This is the later approved typography change; the V3 source-data and model behavior are unchanged.
772
