sections.title: gridtop
sections.html:
774## gridtop
775
776
777gridtop schedules a local command for the cleanest complete window in a regional electricity forecast, then passes through its input, output, signals and exit code. Its terminal countdown shows the exact plan and the intensity difference from starting immediately. A private local ledger keeps forecast comparisons; grams appear only when you supply an energy estimate. The original fourteen-region GB map and generation landscape are still here. No account, key, daemon or hosted service.
778
779
780### See it in ten seconds
781
782Requires macOS or Linux, Rust 1.94.0+, a C compiler, and a Unicode terminal. From this folder:
783
784```sh
785./target/release/gridtop run --demo --dry-run --watch --for 2h --watts 800 -- cargo test --release
786```
787
788The local executable is already built. This preview uses the genuine public forecast saved on 1 November 2026 and a clearly labelled hypothetical 800 W load. It computes the plan using the real scheduler and replays its clock; it never starts the command or writes a ledger. Ctrl-C exits. For a fresh checkout, build first with cargo build --release --locked. A personal install is cargo install --path . --locked; nothing is installed globally by the build or tests.
789
790Run ./target/release/gridtop --demo for the original map. There, → changes the forecast time, j/k selects a region, t cycles the themes, v opens the landscape and m returns to the map. Without --demo, the interactive views connect to the live API. A dated preview is explicit while loading; --live-only keeps the screen neutral until live data arrives. The runner's countdown changes only as time passes or a real forecast refreshes; there is no decorative animation.
791
792```sh
793cargo build --release --locked
794export PATH="$PWD/target/release:$PATH"
795gridtop
796gridtop --theme mono
797gridtop --view landscape --no-motion
798gridtop --postcode SW1
799gridtop --region 13
800```
801
802Startup previews are confined to interactive views. Scripting output requires live data or an explicit, permitted recording mode. Recordings can never release jobs.
803
804The map is rasterised from official NESO DNO boundaries at build time, including holes and islands. A 384×768 region-ID mask is embedded in the executable. Runtime scaling preserves British National Grid proportions and uses terminal half-blocks; no geometry service or browser is needed. The source DNO IDs differ from Carbon Intensity IDs: the explicit join and public city-coordinate tests prevent a London polygon from receiving another region’s forecast. Numbered markers locate regions; they do not represent power stations. There are no drawn power flows.
805
806A comfortable terminal is 164×50. The 44×48 layout keeps all 14 regions visible on a phone-sized terminal. Smaller terminals scroll the regional list around the selection; below 28×22 the map gives a clear size notice. now --json works without an interactive terminal.
807
808The v2.1 plots use filled eighth-block bars. At 80×24, three regional rows stay visible with the scroll hint in the header. Monochrome at 80×24 and all checks.
809
810### Carbon-aware runner
811
812```sh
813gridtop run --region 13 --within 12h --for 2h --watts 800 -- cargo test --release
814gridtop run --postcode SW1 --within 24h --for 45m --dry-run -- python3 -m compileall .
815gridtop next --region 13 --within 12h --for 2h --json
816gridtop runs
817gridtop runs --json
818```
819
820run and next default to London (13), one hour of expected runtime, within 24 hours.
821All fourteen mapped regions and public outward postcode lookup work. The map's old scripting commands
822remain national by default. Use either --within (up to 48h) or --deadline. A deadline is an RFC3339
823instant with Z or an explicit offset, for example 2026-11-03T18:00:00+00:00. Bare local times are
824rejected: the repeated hour at the autumn DST change must not silently pick the wrong instant. Output
825is UTC. A distant deadline is bounded by the available 48h forecast.
826
827The whole expected runtime must fit. Starts are API half-hour boundaries at or after planning time;
828ends may be mid-slot when --for is not a multiple of 30 minutes. The start is fixed once chosen.
829While waiting, the screen stays responsive and refreshes at most once per minute. The displayed
830forecast updates while its original immediate-start baseline is retained. The final launch gate
831checks freshness, area, coverage, lateness and the deadline again. It refuses a start missed by a
832minute, or an expected finish beyond the deadline. Allow scheduling slack for network and OS latency.
833
834--for is an expected runtime, not a timeout: the runner does not kill a job when it reaches that
835length. The comparison assumes constant load over that duration. Ctrl-C while waiting cancels without
836spawning. During execution the child gets the foreground terminal and its original argument array;
837there is no shell interpolation. Its stdin/stdout/stderr pass through. SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 sent to gridtop are
838forwarded to the child's process group, including grandchildren. Keyboard Ctrl-C goes directly to the
839foreground child, avoiding duplicate delivery. Foreground ownership and original terminal settings
840are restored afterwards. The child's exit code passes through, including 128 + signal. This is not a full shell job-control
841manager: a Ctrl-Z/fg/bg suspension workflow is not supported.
842
843--dry-run prints a plan, with --json for a machine-readable one; it never starts a command or
844writes a ledger. --watch adds the interactive dry-run countdown. --demo is allowed only with
845--dry-run on run; it is also available for next. A recording remains marked throughout.
846
847A failed fetch, invalid forecast or failed launch gate is an explicit error. **Only
848--now-if-unavailable permits immediate execution after an acquisition failure.** This opt-in never
849turns a recording, impossible schedule or invalid deadline into permission to run. An immediate
850fallback has no intensity or emissions estimate. There is no silent fallback.
851
852#### Method and estimates
853
854The technique is temporal shifting, also used by the
855Green Software Foundation Carbon Aware SDK.
856Gridtop implements its own exact search in schedule.rs over the
857official regional Carbon Intensity API.
858For each feasible API slot start it integrates the piecewise-constant forecast over the complete
859expected runtime. The minimum wins; ties choose the earliest start. This is exhaustive optimization
860on the supplied forecast, not a learned predictor or a promise about future generation.
861
862```text
863average(t) = sum(forecast_i × seconds_overlapping_slot_i) / expected_runtime_seconds
864avoided intensity = average(start immediately) - average(chosen window)
865estimated grams = avoided intensity × supplied or derived kWh
866kWh from watts = supplied watts × expected_runtime_seconds / 3,600,000
867```
868
869The immediate-start comparison begins at the exact planning instant, including partial edge slots.
870A negative difference stays negative: delaying can be forecast to increase intensity. Energy and
871intensity are separate inputs, as in the operational-emissions term of the
872Software Carbon Intensity methodology. This tool does not
873claim a full SCI score: it does not estimate embodied emissions or a functional unit.
874
875--kwh supplies expected total energy; --watts assumes constant power over --for. Both are explicit
876assumptions. Neither is measured by gridtop. No energy input means no grams. The ledger compares
877its initial baseline with the launch-time forecast; revisions can affect that estimate. A child that
878finishes early, runs longer or fails does not magically acquire a measured energy reading. Actual
879runtime and exit status are recorded separately. No historical grid verification or measured savings
880are claimed. This compares forecast average consumption intensity, not marginal dispatch effects or
881causally verified avoided emissions. The independent minute-resolution oracle covers 300 scheduling cases.
882
883#### Local run ledger
884
885The state directory is $GRIDTOP_STATE_DIR, else $XDG_STATE_HOME/gridtop, else
886$HOME/.local/state/gridtop. Paths must be absolute. Tests and recordings override this into the
887project's .tmp/; they never read or write a real home ledger. Records use private permissions and
888one atomic, synced file per run, with queued, starting, running and terminal states. A failed initial
889ledger write blocks launch. A post-run write error is reported without replacing the child's exit code.
890
891Only the executable's basename, plan, timestamps, status, exit code and forecast estimates are stored.
892Arguments, environment, stdin and child output are never logged. runs shows the last recorded
893state; a hard kill or machine shutdown can leave an unfinished record. There is no background daemon,
894resume service or unattended restart after a crash.
895
896The new screenshots, native demo recordings, scores and performance are in
897DONE-V3.md and shots/v3/. The original map's evidence stays in shots/v2/ and shots/v2.1/.
898
899### Controls
900
901Key / input · Action
902| --- | --- |
903j/k, ↑/↓, mouse wheel · Select a region
904←/→, h/l · Inspect the preceding/next half-hour
905Home / End · Follow the active interval / inspect the final interval
906p · Play/stop forecast frames, one real half-hour per second
907Click map or region row · Select a region
908Click timeline · Select a forecast time
909t, or click the theme name · Phosphor → amber → monochrome
910m / v · Map / landscape
911Tab / Shift+Tab · Move visible focus between map, regions and timeline
912Space · Pause/resume landscape motion
913[ / ] · Cleanest window duration, 1–6 hours
914r · Queue a refresh; the 60-second request floor still applies
915? / Esc · Open / close help
916q / Ctrl+C · Quit and restore terminal modes, cursor and mouse capture
917
918--no-motion or GRIDTOP_REDUCED_MOTION=1 freezes the landscape and disables automatic forecast playback. NO_COLOR selects monochrome in the TUI. There is no flashing or idle map animation. Terminal frames use synchronized-update sequences where supported and ordinary terminal diffing elsewhere. Unknown terminals simply ignore the synchronization hint.
919
920The map, numbers and selected-region detail use the same forecast interval. The bars run from the first to last API interval and share a vertical scale. Each column preserves the highest forecast of its underlying half-hour slots and uses that slot’s API band colour. Reversed blocks overlap each region’s cleanest window (including windows narrower than a column); this marker also works in monochrome. The triangle above the bars marks the selected half-hour. A horizontal baseline means a true zero; missing data stays blank. The map colours use the API’s intensity bands, which are supplied by the provider. In monochrome, the selected-region band is also written in words, and every region has a numeric reading.
921
922### Scripts and scheduling
923
924```sh
925gridtop now
926gridtop now --json
927gridtop best --within 12h --duration 2h
928gridtop best --within 12h --duration 90m --json
929gridtop --region 13 now --json
930gridtop wait --below 100 -- python3 -c 'print("condition met")'
931gridtop wait --cleanest-within 12h -- python3 -c 'print("forecast window reached")'
932```
933
934The one-shot commands remain national by default. The map opens with London selected; that selected region is named in its detail and highlighted in the list. --region 1..14 selects a mapped region. Aggregate regions 15–17 open their generation landscape; they also work with now, best and wait. Postcode lookup is public and keyless. SW1 explicitly resolves to SW1A in London because the API rejects SW1; outward codes such as RG10 are accepted. The original small one-shot demo recordings cover GB and London; the v2 map recording covers all 14 regions.
935
936Durations are whole minutes or hours, 1 minute to 48 hours. Every best-window start is an API half-hour boundary at or after now. The full requested duration must fit inside both the horizon and available forecast. A 45-minute duration can end mid-slot; a two-hour duration starts and ends on half-hours. The lowest time-weighted average wins; ties choose the earliest start. If no complete aligned window fits, the command errors instead of moving the horizon. CLI, TUI and cleanest-wait share this implementation. A 300-case independent oracle checks it.
937
938wait --below uses the active interval’s forecast, strictly less than the threshold, with data fetched less than five minutes ago. wait --cleanest-within selects one complete 30-minute window, counts down, and launches at its start with current data available. Offline or stale data holds the command. Expiry errors without launching. A recording cannot release a command. Interrupting a held command exits 130. Keep the process running: this is a local gate, not a durable scheduler.
939
940The child is spawned through std::process::Command with a literal argument array, never an interpolated shell. Its exit code is returned, including 128 + signal on Unix. Forecasts are estimates; gridtop does not promise emissions savings.
941
942### Data, provenance and failure states
943
944All API requests are read-only HTTPS to api.carbonintensity.org.uk, with rustls, OS trust roots, no redirects or proxies, a 5-second connection timeout, a 15-second request timeout, and a 2 MiB body limit. The map uses one /regional/intensity/{UTC datetime}/fw48h request per minute. Postcode/aggregate selection also uses the relevant reading endpoint. The original CLI uses /intensity, /intensity/{from}/fw48h, /generation and regional/postcode endpoints. Normal builds never fetch data.
945
946The all-region parser requires all 14 mapped regions in all 96 contiguous half-hours, unique known IDs, consistent names, valid timestamps and intensity bands, plausible values, all nine unique fuels, finite 0–100 percentages, and generation totals within rounding tolerance. It never silently fills a missing region with zero. Extra aggregate IDs are recognised and excluded from the map.
947
948- Connecting: a genuine, dated recording keeps the engine visible and says RECORDING … connecting. It never says LIVE DATA before a validated live response.
949- Live-only / slow: --live-only keeps the map neutral and values -- until data arrives; elapsed waiting time is explicit.
950- Empty / API error: no invented values; the error is visible and the map stays neutral.
951- Failed refresh: the last successful forecast remains, with an OFFLINE label and its saved date.
952- Old data: STALE is explicit. An intentionally inspected future interval stays labelled FORECAST.
953- Recording: its real saved date stays visible; no date shifting or automatic demo fallback.
954
955All data times are UTC. Regional generation mix describes consumption including imports, not demand, capacity or physical flows. Colours are forecasts of intensity, not simulated weather. See fixture provenance, atlas-provenance.json, and boundary provenance.
956
957### Checks and evidence
958
959```sh
960cargo fmt --check
961cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
962cargo test --locked
963cargo fetch --locked
964python3 scripts/check_licenses.py
965cargo build --release --locked --examples --bin gridtop
966python3 scripts/pty_check.py
967cargo run --release --locked --example render-bench
968cargo run --release --locked --example v2-gallery -- pass-2
969cargo run --release --locked --example runner-gallery -- pass-2
970python3 scripts/runner-native.py
971cargo run --release --locked --example runner-bench
972```
973
974CI checks Linux and macOS without live API calls or publishing. It is authored locally; remote CI has not been dispatched. Development builds disable incremental debug artifacts to keep rebuildable cache size modest.
975
976shots/v2/ contains two visual critique passes at 1440×900 and 390×844, an actual terminal recording, lifecycle checks, browser reports and native rendering measurements. CRITIQUE.md records defects found and changes made. The screenshots render ratatui content and colours through local HTML, with Plex roles for prose and signs. They are not a separate web implementation. Actual interaction and cleanup are checked independently with TestBackend, mouse/keyboard events and native pseudo terminals.
977
978The optional screenshot harness uses only the installed Playwright package explicitly permitted by the brief. Browser downloads may be kept under .tmp/browsers; no application code from another project is read or reused:
979
980```sh
981node scripts/v2-screenshots.mjs chromium pass-2
982PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.tmp/browsers" node scripts/v2-screenshots.mjs webkit pass-2
983PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.tmp/browsers" node scripts/v2-screenshots.mjs firefox pass-2
984```
985
986Typography now follows the shared IBM Plex family: Sans for reading/interface text,
987Mono for data/code/records, and Sans Condensed for the wordmark and labels. The optional HTML
988capture surface embeds the eight local WOFF2 faces from fonts/ (165,476 bytes before embedding),
989uses font-display: swap, and preloads three main faces. Its cell geometry stays fixed during a
990font swap. There are no runtime font requests. See FONT-LICENCES.md and
991DONE-PLEX.md for provenance, layout measurements and before/after evidence.
992
993To regenerate the current Plex evidence, run the three galleries with an explicit output folder,
994then the browser harness. Coordinate the shared browser slot first; the harness also refuses to
995launch while an automated browser engine is visible in ps.
996
997```sh
998cargo run --locked --example runner-gallery -- plex shots/plex/after/runner
999cargo run --locked --example v2-gallery -- plex shots/plex/after/map
1000cargo run --locked --example v2_1-gallery -- plex shots/plex/after/themes
1001python3 scripts/check-plex.py
1002node scripts/plex-screenshots.mjs chromium
1003PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.tmp/browsers" node scripts/plex-screenshots.mjs webkit
1004PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.tmp/browsers" node scripts/plex-screenshots.mjs firefox
1005```
1006
1007The native TUI uses the terminal emulator's configured font. Select **IBM Plex Mono regular 400
1008and bold 600** there to match the data typography; gridtop cannot set the host's font or mix Sans
1009and Condensed inside a terminal. No global font installation or terminal setting is changed.
1010
1011The capture pages ship zero JavaScript. Their browser checks establish correct evidence rendering, not native TUI compatibility with browsers. og.png is a 1200×630 capture of the real runner using the dated public forecast. favicon.svg is generated from the same boundary raster. Nothing is served or published. Full results, performance numbers and remaining weaknesses are in DONE-V2.md.
1012
1013Reproduce the v2.1 theme/size captures and actual native recordings:
1014
1015```sh
1016cargo run --locked --example v2_1-gallery -- pass-2
1017node scripts/v2_1-screenshots.mjs chromium pass-2
1018python3 scripts/v2-tour.py --output shots/v2.1/wide
1019python3 scripts/v2-tour.py --output shots/v2.1/compact --width 80 --height 24
1020```
1021
1022The new evidence and two-pass critique are in shots/v2.1/; the original v2 evidence stays dated and separate.
1023
1024Short excerpt from the actual recorded terminal:
1025
1026```text
1027gridtop / GB regional carbon intensity
1028RECORDING · 01 Nov 2026
1029FORECAST 01 Nov 15:30–16:00 UTC
1030
103113 London 245 gCO₂/kWh · very high
1032Wind 5.8% Solar 3.6% Gas 57.7% Imports 15.6%
1033Cleanest 2h Mon 04:00–06:00 UTC 49 g/kWh

1051## Listen to the Grid
1052
1053
1054Great Britain's electricity grid, played live as an orchestral score. Each source of power has its own staff and
1055its own voice: wind is a string pad, solar rings bells, gas holds a low drone, nuclear keeps a steady pulse, hydro
1056runs like water, biomass sings, imports arrive as distant chords, and coal (should it ever return) is grit. Each
1057plays louder the bigger its share of generation, and carbon intensity chooses the key: a clean grid plays in bright
1058modes, a dirty one turns minor. The score is engraved as you listen, a note inked the moment it sounds. Pick any
1059day since 12 May 2018 and the page presses it as a record: a minute of audio rendered in your browser, with the
1060day's own score as its sleeve.
1061
1062
1063### Quickstart
1064
1065Needs Node 22.12 or later.
1066
1067```sh
1068npm ci
1069npm run dev
1070```
1071
1072Open the address Vite prints (http://localhost:5173 unless that port is busy) and press Listen. To build the
1073static site and serve it as it would be deployed:
1074
1075```sh
1076npm run build
1077npm run preview
1078```
1079
1080dist/ is plain static files (about 71 kB of gzipped JavaScript, plus a 1.5 kB loudness worker) and can be hosted anywhere. To build beside a
1081dist/ that is being served, use npx vite build --outDir dist-next and test it with DIST=dist-next npm run shots. Link to a region with
1082?region=north-scotland, ?region=london and so on (the slugs are in src/data/regions.ts).
1083
1084### Any day, pressed as a record
1085
1086Choose a day under Any day, pressed as a record and press. The page fetches that day from NESO (two requests;
1087yesterday is already on the page and costs none), composes it one bar an hour (23, 24 or 25 bars, whatever the
1088clocks did), engraves the sleeve, then renders the same bars offline with the same engine the page plays live,
1089faster than real time. You get:
1090
1091- a 16-bit, 44.1 kHz stereo WAV of about a minute, with its title, artist, date and data credit inside it (RIFF
1092INFO and an ID3 tag) and the sleeve embedded as cover art;
1093- the sleeve as a 2400 px PNG: the day's score as the first page of a printed edition, in three systems of eight
1094bars (night, day, evening), each bar labelled with its hour;
1095- liner notes on the page: how many half-hours NESO had, the cleanest hour, the journey of keys.
1096
1097The same date and place always press the same record. Rendering takes about 3 seconds in WebKit, 5 to 12 seconds in
1098Chromium and about a minute in Firefox, whose offline audio runs at roughly real time (it shows a running count
1099instead of a percentage, since Firefox doesn't report progress).
1100
1101### Ossia: fully renewable
1102
1103An ossia is the engraver's alternative passage, printed in small staves above the music. Press **Ossia: fully
1104renewable** (or O) and the moment you are hearing is re-scored for a hypothetical grid that runs on wind, sun and
1105water alone:
1106
1107- gas, coal, nuclear, biomass, imports and other are set to zero, and their share is handed to wind, solar and hydro
1108in proportion to each one's real share that half-hour (src/music/ossia.ts);
1109- if a half-hour had no wind, sun or water at all, there is nothing to scale up, so the ossia gives the whole grid to
1110wind, the renewable that can run at any hour;
1111- NESO's factors for wind, solar and hydro are 0 g CO₂/kWh, so the ossia is 0 g and the key ladder puts it in D
1112Lydian, luminoso.
1113
1114Both versions of every bar are always composed, by two conductors in step, so switching is instant and mid-bar: the
1115sound changes without a restart and you hear the same moment real and renewable. The ossia is printed over the live
1116bar (over every bar of a replayed day), labelled ossia: fully renewable, hypothetical, and the rule and its
1117numbers (real mix against ossia mix, real grams against 0 g, real key against Lydian) appear under the controls. It
1118never appears in the Live label or the live bar's time. Pressed with the ossia on, a record is the ossia's: its
1119sleeve engraves only wind, solar and hydro, says ossia and hypothetical and marks the other parts tacet, and its
1120file names and tags say so too.
1121
1122#### A fair A/B: loudness matching with ITU-R BS.1770
1123
1124Louder sounds better to most ears, and the ossia, with its big wind and solar parts and a brighter key, measures 1.8
1125to 2.7 LU louder than the real grid across the sample day. So the two are loudness-matched before you compare them,
1126with the broadcast standard's integrated loudness,
1127ITU-R BS.1770-4 (src/audio/loudness.ts): K-weighting (a high shelf for
1128the head and a 38 Hz high pass), mean square over 400 ms blocks overlapping by 75%, an absolute gate at −70 LUFS and a
1129relative gate 10 LU below, then the gated mean. It is tested against the standard's own 48 kHz filter coefficients
1130and the EBU Tech 3341 reference signals (cases 1 to 4, both gates).
1131
1132- Live, per moment (src/audio/match.ts, src/ossia-loudness.ts). When the ossia is on, the page renders the
1133moment both ways offline, in your browser, sixteen bars each at 48 kHz, measures each, and trims the ossia to the
1134real grid's loudness; the real grid keeps its own level. A replay is matched hour by hour, measuring the next hour
1135ahead. While listening to the real grid it measures in the background, so switching is usually matched at once;
1136until a moment is measured the last trim carries over, or, before any, the typical −2.2 dB, labelled provisional.
1137The arithmetic runs in a worker. A measurement takes about 1.5 to 7 seconds depending on the browser and the
1138machine, and the panel shows both loudnesses, the trims and the time it took.
1139- How fair. At every other half-hour of the sample day the page's own measurement set the trim, and an
1140independent render of the same moment (other notes) checked it: the trimmed ossia and the real grid differ by
11410.06 LU at the median and 0.25 LU at most (node scripts/measure-audio.mjs --loudness).
1142- Records. Every pressed record, real or ossia, is measured and pressed to −16 LUFS (or as near as keeps its
1143sample peak under −1 dBFS), and its liner notes and tags say so. The browser checks re-measure the downloaded WAV
1144files in Node with the same meter.
1145
1146Why not give each fuel its own key, fossil fuels minor and renewables major, sounding at once? Major and minor
1147thirds played together clash. The grid-wide key already says it: the cleaner the grid, the brighter the key, from D
1148Lydian below 60 g CO₂/kWh to D Phrygian from 240 g.
1149
1150### How it works
1151
1152```
1153NESO Carbon Intensity API ──> zod schemas ──> half-hour series ──> arrange() ──> Conductor (a bar at a time)
1154 (or bundled sample) src/data src/data src/music src/music
1155 ├──> AudioEngine (live, or offline for records)
1156 └──> engraver ──> live score / sleeve
1157```
1158
1159- Data (src/data, src/feed.ts). National figures from /generation and /intensity, the week from
1160/generation/{from}/{to} and /intensity/{from}/{to}, regions from /regional/regionid/{id} and
1161/regional/intensity/{from}/{to}/regionid/{id}. Every response is validated with zod, cached copies included.
1162The page polls a few minutes after each half-hour is due, keeps the week in localStorage for 25 minutes, and
1163enforces its network allowlist with a Content-Security-Policy: scripts, styles and fonts from the page itself,
1164data from NESO, nothing else.
1165- Composition (src/music). Pure, seeded functions. Amplitude is the square root of a fuel's share. Intensity
1166picks one of six modes on D (Lydian under 60 g to Phrygian from 240 g, with 5 g of hysteresis). The conductor
1167writes a whole bar at a time in eight-bar phrases: one chord a bar, a half cadence at bar four and home to D at
1168bar eight, a sung motif that repeats and answers itself, bells that reply in the voice's gaps, and a swell across
1169each phrase that the engine plays and the score marks as hairpins. Every note is in the bar's key, so the score
1170never needs an accidental.
1171- Type. One family, IBM Plex: Sans to read, Mono for data and records (the times over the bars, bar numbers,
1172figures, liner notes), Sans Condensed for signs (the wordmark, headings, instrument names). Noto Music draws the
1173notation, which Plex does not have. All self-hosted with font-display: swap. The first screen is set in three
1174faces (Sans 400, Sans 500, Condensed 600), and those three are preloaded, so nothing moves when they arrive:
1175layout shift measures 0.00000 at 1440×900 and 390×844 (it was 0.0009 and 0.0013 with the old Google-hosted type).
1176The canvases wait for every face they draw in before engraving. One quirk of the test setup: the preloads carry
1177crossorigin, as the Fetch standard loads fonts, and Chromium and Firefox reuse them. Served by Vite's preview
1178server, which answers with Vary: Origin and Cache-Control: no-cache, WebKit did not: it fetched those three
1179faces twice and logged a warning (it reused them only without crossorigin, which Chromium then refuses). On a
1180plain static server without those headers, WebKit reused the same preloads once with no warning, so the headers
1181are the likely cause, not WebKit generally. The browser checks allow that one WebKit message, for those three
1182files only.
1183- Engraving (src/notation). Rhythm spelling that respects the beat and the middle of the bar, ties, rests,
1184beams, stems, ledger lines, octave clefs, modal key signatures (D Lydian is three sharps, D Phrygian two flats)
1185with double bar lines and cancelling naturals when the key changes, dynamics where they change, entry marks
1186(l.v., pizz., lontano), tempo and bar numbers. Clefs, rests, accidentals and dynamics are real glyphs from
1187Noto Music. The live page is one system that reads through the last two hours, a bar a half-hour: the
1188half-hours already past are engraved whole from their own figures (composed from midnight with a seed from the day
1189and place, so a half-hour's bar never changes as the page moves on), and the last bar is the live half-hour, inked
1190note by note as it sounds, with a red cursor following. Its bar numbers count the day's half-hours (17:00 is bar
119135). Hairpins are drawn bar by bar, so a swell can cross a bar line and stops at any new dynamic. A replayed day is
1192written an hour a bar on pages that fill and turn.
1193- Sound (src/audio). A hand-written Web Audio graph: detuned-saw drone, four-voice pad with portamento, FM
1194bells, a felt pulse, a formant singer, filtered-noise water, plucks and grit; per-voice buses with a phrase
1195expression stage; a generated convolution reverb; then high-pass, tone, a light glue compressor, a limiter and a
1196soft clip. Every data change is a ramp.
1197- Honesty. The page says whether a figure is measured or forecast, which half-hour it is, when it was checked,
1198and that regional figures are modelled. The score's earlier bars are half-hours NESO published, never filled in
1199across a gap; while the week is loading, or if it fails, they stay empty and say so. Only the newest half-hour is
1200called live, in red; a late one is the latest, and a held or recorded one carries its time alone. Offline it
1201plays src/data/sample-day.json, a real recording of Wednesday 28 October 2026, labelled with that date and never
1202called live.
1203
1204### Checks
1205
1206```sh
1207npm run check # typecheck, lint, unit tests, dependency licences
1208npm run measure # renders the instrument offline: levels, clipping, clicks, phrasing, brightness
1209npm run shots # every state at 1440×900 and 390×844 into shots/v2/, with checks in Chromium, WebKit, Firefox
1210node scripts/perf.mjs # first engraved paint and frame cost during a replay, in all three browsers
1211npm run silence # proves the automation is silent: no browser it drives holds a macOS audio assertion
1212```
1213
1214Every browser these scripts drive is silent and opens no audio device: scripts/silent.mjs gives the page a live
1215AudioContext with no output (an OfflineAudioContext that is never rendered, keeping real time), and adds
1216--mute-audio in Chromium and a zero volume scale in Firefox. Records and measurements render offline to memory,
1217as they always do.
1218
1219The unit tests assert concrete values for the tricky core: API schemas against real responses, UK days across
1220clock changes, the scale quantiser, voice leading, the mapping, the conductor (in key, spellable rhythms, phrases
1221that come home, a steady pulse), rhythm spelling, staff positions and key signatures, hairpins and ties across
1222bar lines, the half-hours before now (gaps never bridged, a past bar unchanged as the page moves on), the ossia's
1223mix (shares sum to 1, zero fossil and other, proportions kept, the fallback, Lydian at 0 g), whole-day composition,
1224BS.1770 loudness (the standard's filter coefficients, EBU Tech 3341 cases 1 to 4, gain tracking, silence), the
1225ossia's trim and the record level, the matcher's queue, the WAV and ID3 writer, the reverb impulse and the readouts. npm run shots and scripts/perf.mjs use Playwright, a
1226dev dependency here (npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox once).
1227
1228shots/v2/yesterday.wav is a real record pressed by the page: Saturday 31 October 2026.
1229
1230### Dependencies
1231
1232One runtime dependency, zod (MIT), run in jitless mode so the page can forbid eval. Build and test tools: Vite,
1233Vitest, TypeScript, ESLint, typescript-eslint and Playwright. npm run licences checks every installed package
1234against MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD and ISC. Keeping that true needs two pins: ESLint stays on 9.x and typescript-eslint on
12358.56 (later versions need a BlueOak-licensed minimatch), and argparse is pinned to its MIT 1.x (ESLint pulls in the
1236Python-licensed 2.x through js-yaml, which uses it only for its own command line). The cost is one moderate npm
1237advisory (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249) in that dev-only lint toolchain. Production dependencies audit clean.
1238

1242formerly National Grid ESO), licensed under CC BY 4.0 and used
1243under its API terms.
1244- Type: IBM Plex (Sans, Mono and Sans Condensed) and
1245Noto Music, both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 and served from the
1246page itself (public/fonts/, from @fontsource 5.3.0): no font requests leave the site. Each file, its size, source
1247and licence are listed in LICENCES.md.
1248

sections.html:
1254## Sourced
1255
1256
1257An interactive calculation pad where every number carries a unit, a source and, if it is uncertain, a cited or assumed spread. The answer is then a distribution, not one number: drag a quantity and 4,096 Monte Carlo runs redraw in the same frame; let go and 100,000 runs and a variance-based (Sobol) sensitivity analysis show which uncertainty actually matters. Sourced is a hand-written TypeScript language with dimensional analysis, provenance DAGs, an interpreter, a JavaScript compiler and a column-wise Monte Carlo evaluator. Everything runs locally in your browser; there are no accounts, uploads, remote models or runtime external requests.
1258
1259### Try it
1260
1261Node 22.13 or later is required. From this folder:
1262
1263```sh
1264npm ci --ignore-scripts
1265npm run dev
1266```
1267
1268Open http://127.0.0.1:4177. In ten seconds: the commute opens with 70.88 kg of CO₂ and, under it, the distribution of 100,000 runs: 90% between about 56 and 87 kg. The sentence above the sensitivity table says what matters: knowing your fuel consumption exactly would remove about 81% of the variance, while IPCC’s published uncertainty on its factors accounts for about 4%. Drag the underlined 0.065 and the hatched distribution moves with it, every frame; release and it refines. Then open Rooftop solar: with every input at its average, the payback is 9.86 years, but the average payback is longer, because a ratio of uncertain quantities is not the ratio of their averages.
1269
1270The Adjust select and numeric field are the keyboard alternative. Arrow keys step the selected quantity. While dragging, Alt is 100× finer, Shift is 10× coarser, and Escape cancels. The ends of a range are draggable too. CodeMirror undo/redo remains available; each example keeps its own history. Page numbers, publication years, coverage and round precision are syntax, not data inputs. Edits stay in memory; refreshing restores the examples.
1271
1272For a production build served locally:
1273
1274```sh
1275npm run build
1276npm run preview -- --port 4177 --strictPort
1277```
1278
1279Open http://127.0.0.1:4177. Both servers bind only to loopback. Installation uses the public npm registry. The app needs no network connection once loaded; its fonts are served from this folder, never from a font service.
1280
1281### The small language
1282
1283```sourced
1284source invoice.march = "Example invoice, March 2026", page 2
1285let usage = 284 kWh @invoice.march
1286assume tariff = 0.25 £/kWh
1287
1288fn charge(energy, price) = energy * price
1289let cost = round(charge(usage, tariff), 2)
1290print "Electricity: {cost}"
1291```
1292
1293This prints Electricity: £71.00. Its lineage contains both @invoice.march and the explicit tariff assumption. let count = 14200 is an error: add a unit and a declared source, or use assume.
1294
1295Any quantity can also say how uncertain it is, and who says so:
1296
1297```sourced
1298let emission = 69300 kg/TJ @ipcc ~ 95% 67500..73000 @ipcc
1299assume density = 0.74 kg/L ~ ±0.025 kg/L assumed
1300assume consumption = 0.065 L/km ~ normal(12%) assumed
1301assume daily = 24 km ~ ±2 km assumed
1302```
1303
1304A spread without @source or assumed is an error, as is one that excludes its own value, uses an incompatible unit or names an undeclared source. ±w and low..high state limits only, so they are uniform: the GUM’s rule when only bounds are known (JCGM 100:2008 §4.3.7). 95% low..high states a coverage interval, such as a published confidence interval: Sourced draws a two-piece normal whose mode stays at the value and which puts exactly that share of runs between the limits. normal(sd), lognormal(factor) (median at the value, geometric standard deviation), triangular(low, high) (mode at the value) and uniform(low, high) name a shape outright. In ± and normal(), a percentage is relative to the value; elsewhere a bound without a unit uses the quantity’s unit and a bound with a unit is converted.
1305
1306- Declarations: source, let, assume, fn; display results with interpolated print strings. Statements end at newlines or semicolons. Comments start with //.
1307- Source metadata: a title and optional page 2, year 2006, url "https://…". HTTP/HTTPS links are validated, never fetched by the app, and open only when selected.
1308- Arithmetic: + - * /, unary signs and parentheses. Addition/subtraction convert compatible units; mismatched dimensions are errors. as converts a whole expression: (a * b) as kg.
1309- Lists and built-ins: sum([first, second]), sqrt(area), round(total, 2). Rounding ties follow JavaScript’s Math.round (toward positive infinity). Rounding precision is literal syntax from 0 to 8, not a data input. Other unsourced literals are allowed only inside an explicit assume declaration.
1310- Units: SI base units m kg s A K mol cd; g mg t km mi cm mm min h day year J kJ MJ GJ TJ Wh kWh W kW L mL £ % ratio, and the multiplicative named SI derived units Hz N Pa C V F Ω ohm S Wb T H lm lx Bq Gy Sv kat rad sr. Absolute Celsius requires affine arithmetic and is deliberately excluded; use kelvin. A year is 365.25 days. ratio is the explicit dimensionless unit for sourced values.
1311- Compound units: kg/kWh, £/day, kg*m^2/s^2. Exponents are exact reduced rationals, including m^(1/2); each written exponent numerator is from −32 to 32 and denominator from 1 to 32.
1312- Functions capture earlier definitions and are unit polymorphic: the body is dimension-checked for each call. Named function calls use the function namespace; parameters are values, not callable function objects. Bindings are immutable. Recursion, control flow, strings as data values, external I/O and imports are intentionally outside the language.
1313
1314A mismatch is explained at its exact source span:
1315
1316```text
1317Units don’t add up at 4:13
13184 | let total = energy + mass
1319 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
1320You’re adding kWh to kg.
1321Did you mean to multiply by an emission factor (kg/kWh)?
1322```
1323
1324There is no stale success state: an invalid program clears the previous results. Parser recovery preserves later declarations. The checker suppresses diagnostics caused by an already-failed binding while still reporting independent errors.
1325
1326### How it works
1327
1328src/lang/ contains a hand-written lexer and Pratt/recursive-descent parser, a separate checker, rational dimension algebra, an AST interpreter and a JavaScript emitter. No parser generator, model, server or remote API is involved.
1329
1330A quantity carries a magnitude, a unit (scale and dimension vector) and a node in an immutable lineage DAG. Operations retain the exact input edges and union their distinct source/assumption dependencies. The technical schematic preserves the calculation DAG, including shared inputs, conversions and rounding, while collapsing transparent aliases. Deep derivations are drawn vertically and can be panned and zoomed. Source nodes point back to declared metadata and the original code spans.
1331
1332The compiler emits JavaScript against the exported createRuntime() operations. It uses generated identifiers and JSON-escaped metadata, and never incorporates user identifiers as JavaScript identifiers. In TypeScript/Node, the backend can be used like this:
1333
1334```ts
1335import { parse, compile, createRuntime } from './src/lang';
1336
1337const body = compile(parse(programText)); // rejects invalid programs
1338const evaluate = new Function('rt', body); // Node-side only
1339const result = evaluate(createRuntime());
1340console.log(result.outputs);
1341```
1342
1343The browser never evaluates generated JavaScript. “See JavaScript” exposes the emitted code for inspection; the live results use the interpreter. Tests execute the generated backend in Node and compare every output, binding, dependency and lineage node with the interpreter.
1344
1345The playground uses CodeMirror 6, TypeScript, and plain DOM/SVG rendering. Its identity comes from engineering calculation pads and technical schematics: white, graphite, cobalt traces, orange lower-input scenarios, measured rules and orthogonal wires. See IDENTITY.md. The served HTML reserves the final pad geometry while the editor and local worker load. The worker is bundled inline to avoid a second startup fetch.
1346
1347### Answers as distributions
1348
1349Monte Carlo propagation (JCGM 101:2008, the GUM’s Supplement 1). Each run draws every uncertain input from its declared distribution and recomputes the whole program; the spread of answers is the result’s distribution. The page reports P5, P50 and P95 (Hyndman and Fan’s type-7 quantiles, the R and NumPy default), the mean, and the answer from central inputs, all in the result’s own unit.
1350
1351The trick that makes 100,000 runs cheap is that units are static. The checker has already proven every dimension, so src/analysis/columns.ts evaluates the checked syntax tree once per operation over a whole column of runs (Float64Arrays), resolving each unit conversion once instead of 100,000 times. It mirrors the interpreter’s arithmetic in the same order, and a test proves it reproduces the scalar interpreter bit for bit on every example, including decimal rounding (a fast path defers to the interpreter’s exact routine near ties). A run that divides by zero or takes a negative square root is counted as undefined and excluded, never folded into the answer. One literal is one random variable, even when a function uses it twice.
1352
1353Seeds. Uniforms come from xoshiro128** (Blackman and Vigna) seeded by splitmix32, one named stream per literal, mapped through inverse CDFs (Acklam’s inverse normal). The same seed always gives the same runs. Because each quantity keeps its own stream, dragging one number reuses everyone’s random numbers (common random numbers), so the shape moves instead of flickering. Small programs draw a 4,096-run preview in the same animation frame as the number under the pointer; the worker then refines to 100,000 runs, and the preview’s runs are exactly the first 4,096 of the refined pass. A worker request is coalesced: a newer drag frame supersedes unfinished refinement before any work starts.
1354
1355Variance-based sensitivity (Sobol′ 2001; Saltelli et al. 2010; Jansen 1999). The tornado nudges one input at a time by ±5, 10 or 20%. The variance share asks a different question: how much of the result’s spread comes from each input’s declared uncertainty. With two independent sample matrices A and B and, for each input i, A with column i taken from B, the first-order index Sᵢ = mean(f(B)·(f(A_Bⁱ) − f(A)))/V (Saltelli 2010) is the share of variance that knowing input i exactly would remove; the total index Sₜᵢ = mean((f(A) − f(A_Bⁱ))²)/2V (Jansen 1999) adds every interaction it takes part in. The hatched gap between them is interaction. Outputs are centred first, as Sobol′ recommends; intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over 100 resamples. The design costs (k + 2) × 16,384 runs for k uncertain inputs. Fixed inputs say “fixed”: they have no variance to share. A rule-written sentence above the table states the finding from the numbers on screen.
1356
1357What is live and what is recorded. Everything is live: no run, distribution or index on the page is precomputed. Nothing is downloaded. The limits of the method are stated on the page: inputs are sampled independently (correlations are not modelled), and a distribution is only as good as the spreads declared, which are labelled cited or assumed wherever they appear.
1358
1359#### Measured
1360
1361The tests check the engine against closed forms rather than against itself: a sum of normals in mixed units (km + mi) reproduces its analytic P5/P50/P95 within the quantile standard error; a product of lognormals reproduces its analytic quantiles and mean within 1%; Sobol indices recover an additive model (S = T = ⅕, ⅘, 0) and the product X₁·X₂ of normals, whose interaction is exact (S₁ = 0.889, S₂ = 0.056, T₁ = 0.944, T₂ = 0.111), within 0.03; every distribution reproduces its exact mean and variance; the two-piece normal puts 95% of 200,000 draws between its limits (binomial tolerance); and the xoshiro128** outputs for state (1, 2, 3, 4) match hand-derived reference values.
1362
1363On the bundled examples (100,000 runs, seed 1): the commute’s 90% interval is 55.6–86.7 kg around the 70.88 kg central answer; consumption explains 81% of the variance alone, distance 13%, IPCC’s emission factor 2%, density 2% and IPCC’s calorific value 1%. The solar payback is 9.86 years at central inputs, with a mean of 10.2 and a 90% interval of 7.6–13.6 years; interactions carry about 6% of its variance. Performance is reported in DONE v3.
1364
1365### Scrubbing, sensitivity and tracing
1366
1367- Only a numeric token changes during a scrub. Units, sources and the rest of the program stay intact. Signed, underscored and scientific-notation literals work. Manual numeric edits retain the requested finite IEEE-754 value.
1368- Sensitivity reruns the actual interpreter twice per contributing literal, one input at a time, at ±5%, ±10% or ±20%. All other inputs stay fixed. Negative inputs use the magnitude of the perturbation; a zero input uses one numeric step. Rounded results may have zero change. Undefined perturbations stay labelled.
1369- Inputs are distinct literal sites, not source names: two tariffs from one document remain two inputs. A literal in a function is perturbed once at its definition and affects every use. Unrelated inputs are excluded by the selected result's reachable graph.
1370- Every contributing input is analysed. Small programs (up to 1,000 characters, 100 AST nodes, eight calls and two function declarations) get one interpreter pass per animation frame for immediate numeric feedback. Larger programs and all sensitivity scans run in a dedicated worker. Both paths use the same interpreter; stale worker replies are discarded. Charts initially show the top 48 ranked inputs; “Show all” exposes the complete ranking. Progress counts are explicit for larger programs. The main thread stays available for editing.
1371- Hover or focus a result to highlight the actual derivation tokens, including source declarations and function definitions. Sensitivity rows locate individual inputs. The schematic collapses transparent aliases, retains provenance-changing assumptions, and draws every operation. Drawings reflow across the available width, wrapping inputs on narrow screens. Ordinary Derivation panels grow to show the whole calculation at readable size. Text stays at least 11px even when zooming out; genuinely large derivations use an explicit scroll hint.
1372- Edits to a bundled example are labelled what-if scenarios and compared with its original numeric result when applicable. They do not revise the cited document or imply that a different scientific factor was published.
1373- The tornado probes a value without that literal’s own spread, so a ±10% nudge past a cited interval still measures the value’s effect. Dragging a value past its declared interval is an explicit error, because the declared uncertainty no longer describes it.
1374- An exact result says so and offers one undoable click to add an assumed ±10% spread to its most influential input. Uncertain terminals in the schematic carry a small drawing of their input distribution’s shape: cobalt for cited, orange for assumed. Selecting one names the spread, its shape and its provenance.
1375
1376No UI framework, third-party font service or decorative image assets are used. Type is IBM Plex, self-hosted from public/fonts/ (latin subsets): Sans for reading and interface text, Mono for code and quantities, Sans Condensed for the wordmark, headings, labels and the drawing’s annotations. Faces use font-display: swap. The three seen first (Sans 400, Mono 400, Condensed 600) are preloaded by a three-line script at the top of <head>: WebKit fetches same-origin @font-face fonts without CORS while Chromium and Firefox fetch them with it, and a preload is reused only when its mode matches, so a single static <link rel=preload> downloads twice in one engine or the other. Keyboard paths, visible focus, modal focus management and reduced-motion preferences are supported. Inside the editor Tab indents; Escape releases focus so Tab can reach the next control. Offline status stays visible; calculations continue offline after loading. An unavailable worker produces an explicit uncomputed state, retains the code, and offers a reference or retry action.
1377
1378Bounds keep a local mistake local: 30,000 characters, 128 syntax/AST nesting levels, 32 function-call levels, 10,000 checking steps and 10,000 generated calculation nodes. Dimension exponents remain exact within safe-integer rational representation; out-of-range dimensions and unit scales produce explicit errors. Arithmetic uses finite IEEE-754 numbers rather than arbitrary precision or decimal accounting. Currency display uses at least two and up to six decimals, retaining sub-penny amounts; very small or large values use scientific notation; use round to record rounding as an actual derivation step.
1379
1380### Checks and measurements
1381
1382```sh
1383npm run check # strict typecheck, Biome lint, tests, production build, licence check
1384npm audit --audit-level=moderate --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
1385npm run measure # 200 runs per example, after 20 warmups; writes shots/core-performance.json
1386```
1387
1388The tests cover lexer/parser recovery, precise diagnostics (including escaped-string offsets and every uncertainty error), unit algebra and conversions, lineage propagation, failures and limits, compiler hygiene, and interpreter/JavaScript agreement on all five examples, including uncertain lineage. Deterministic property checks exercise 4,000 scale round trips, 600 round trips through the actual interpreter with provenance intact, 120,000 column-rounding cases against the interpreter’s exact rounding, and bit-for-bit agreement of the column evaluator with the interpreter on 200 perturbed runs across every example. tests/stats.test.ts and tests/uncertainty.test.ts hold the analytic Monte Carlo and Sobol checks described above.
1389
1390Browser verification uses the public Playwright installation named in the brief through createRequire for Chromium, plus this project's pinned Playwright for WebKit and Firefox. Browser binaries are test tools and are not redistributed with the app. The v2 brief explicitly permits installing WebKit/Firefox:
1391
1392```sh
1393PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.cache/browsers" node node_modules/playwright/cli.js install webkit firefox
1394npm run test:browser
1395npm run test:layout
1396npm run test:contrast
1397npm run test:shift
1398npm run measure:browser
1399```
1400
1401Keep the server running. The default test URL is http://127.0.0.1:4177. Set SOURCED_URL to test a separately served production build; node scripts/serve-built.mjs starts an isolated production preview on an OS-assigned loopback port and records its own PID/URL in shots/v3/preview-process.json. It does not stop the existing dev server. For another machine, set SOURCED_PLAYWRIGHT_PACKAGE="$PWD/package.json" and use an installed Chrome with SOURCED_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome, or install that pinned Playwright's Chromium separately.
1402
1403The browser suite runs the complete state and interaction contracts in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, at 1440×900 and 390×844. For v3 it opens on the commute and asserts the 100,000-run distribution brackets the central answer, the cited/assumed spread receipt, the variance finding, fixed inputs and the opening-screen position of the distribution; it drags consumption and requires the preview distribution to be drawn in the same frame as the number with no layout shift, then refinement on release and one-step undo; it drags the upper end of IPCC’s interval and requires P95 to move; it reseeds; it reads a terminal’s spread detail; it checks the exact state and its one-click spread, an invalid spread’s explicit error, and recovery without a stale hint. The v2 contracts follow unchanged: live scrubbing before release, cancellation, keyboard adjustment, dependency tracing, result-specific sensitivity, source inspection, every example, unit errors, empty/long content, undefined scenarios, 60-input ranking, offline operation and dialogs. Slow-load and unsupported-worker fixtures exercise explicit uncomputed states. Browser test scripts assert zero console errors/warnings and no external requests. The layout suite measures actual SVG text bounds through every zoom step for all three outputs of all five examples, and requires every input-distribution glyph to stay clear of every annotation. It checks the complete opening view at both sizes, including the phone tab reveal, a measured 11px minimum text size, width use, panel growth, readable large-diagram scrolling, and native text size when there is sufficient room. It also checks selected-result lineage and scenario comparisons. Ordinary drawings fit their width and grow vertically instead of shrinking into an unreadable overview. Large drawings preserve readable text with a visible scrolling hint. Any scaling still transforms the complete SVG, preserving its native text layout. v3 evidence lives in shots/v3/ (baseline, pass-1, pass-2, performance, contrast, social preview) and its two design critiques in docs/V3-CRITIQUE.md. Earlier evidence remains in shots/v2/, shots/v2.1/, shots/v2.2/ and shots/v2.3/, with docs/V2-CRITIQUE.md.
1404
1405npm run measure:browser records application-marked meaningful paint, the time to the opener’s preview, refined distribution and Sobol shares (with the worker’s own compute time), total gzipped main+worker JavaScript, and frame timing while dragging the commute with its distribution redrawing every frame, alongside idle timing and host load on the same machine. Meaningful paint is the frame after real results are rendered, measured from navigation start; it is an application timing marker, not the retired browser FMP metric. npm run measure records core execution over 200 runs per example after 20 warmups. Contrast checks measure the playground and reference against AA text thresholds; they are not a full accessibility audit. npm run test:shift guards zero layout shift in every engine. The browser layout-shift API exists only in Chromium, so the check also compares each landmark in the static HTML shell (JavaScript blocked, web fonts loaded) with the fully rendered, font-swapped page at both sizes, and fails if any box in the first screen moves. Late content has its room reserved, and the fallback faces are local system fonts sized to Plex’s measured widths and vertical metrics, so the font swap moves nothing. Hosted CI remains unrun in this local-only build.
1406
1407The existing dev server may retain a transform when file events are missed. vite.config.ts enables polling on future starts. node scripts/refresh-dev.mjs uses Vite's own HMR client to refresh this project's served modules without killing a process or changing its port. Production screenshots are taken against the isolated built preview, and the public dev URL is checked separately.
1408
1409### Data and credits
1410
1411Household bills, tariffs, route lengths, pump prices and the original pancake recipe are illustrative, labelled as such in both source declarations and the UI. They are not current prices, client records or live data.
1412
1413The commute example quotes these public numerical facts from the IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 2 (Energy):

1416- Chapter 1, Table 1.2: motor gasoline default net calorific value 44.3 TJ/Gg, equivalent to 44.3 MJ/kg, with published lower and upper values 42.5 and 44.8.

The two-piece normal that keeps the default as the mode is Sourced’s modelling choice, not IPCC’s. The rooftop-solar quote, tariff, generation and every one of its spreads are illustrative assumptions. It estimates combustion CO₂ only: it excludes fuel production, vehicle manufacture, CH₄ and N₂O.
