2137## receipts
2138
2139
2140receipts records local commands, checks an agent’s claims against the current code, and signs recorded evidence so another machine can verify exactly which bytes were endorsed.
2141
2142```sh
2143npm ci
2144npm run demo:attestation
2145node dist/cli.js verify shots/v3/archive.dsse.json --key shots/v3/trusted-public.pem --subject-root shots/v3
2146```
2147
2148Open shots/v3/attestation.html: WebCrypto verifies the public fixture live. Change its recorded exit from 0 to 1; JSON stays valid and the signature fails. Restore the original bytes and it verifies again. This is recorded synthetic input from the real CLI, signed at import—not an execution-time agent signature. Missing execution facts remain explicit nulls.
2149
2150The technique is an in-toto Statement v1, signed over DSSE’s byte encoding with Ed25519. Keys are project-local and ignored. Verification requires an independently trusted public key. A valid signature authenticates bytes, not historical truth or test quality. See the exact CLI, predicate, import and trust contract.
2151
2152### Stop unsupported claims
2153
2154```text
2155$ fake-agent finish "Done. Verification passed."
2156BLOCK No recorded command backs this claim.
2157$ receipts run -- ./verify
2158Tests 3 passed (3)
2159$ fake-agent finish "Done. Verification passed."
2160ALLOW Matching command passed against the current code.
2161$ edit source.mjs
2162$ fake-agent finish "Done. Verification passed."
2163BLOCK Nothing has run since your last edit.
2164```
2165
2166That is the synthetic local demonstration, not a live agent recording. Run it from a fresh clone:
2167
2168```sh
2169npm ci
2170npm run demo
2171```
2172
2173The command prints the full session and saves the terminal capture and a self-contained report at shots/v2/reports/mixed.html. Open that file in a browser (or run npm run preview for a loopback preview at http://127.0.0.1:4318/mixed.html): claims link to their exact command, code identity and captured output. No server or network is needed. Requires Node 22.12+, npm and Git; no account, model or global installation.
2174
2175### Install the stopping gate
2176
2177Build once, then install into a target Git project root:
2178
2179```sh
2180npm run build
2181node /absolute/path/to/receipts/dist/cli.js hook install --project /path/to/project
2182```
2183
2184This merges a Stop handler into the project’s .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json. Choose one with --agent claude or --agent codex. Existing settings survive; repeating the same installation is a no-op. It never reads or writes user configuration. Review the command in the host’s /hooks interface and reload as required. Codex also requires a trusted project configuration layer and manual trust of the exact hook. The installer does not grant trust. See the hook contract and limits, based on the official Claude Code and Codex protocols.
2185
2186The hook checks the supplied final message without opening a transcript. Unsupported claims block with a quoted claim, verdict and next action. Even a bare “Done” needs a fresh aggregate verification receipt. Continuation turns are checked again; a loop flag cannot silently permit stale evidence. This stricter no-claim policy applies to the installed hook; ordinary check continues to report zero recognized claims honestly.
2187
2188Record commands after installation and after the final edit, from the target project:
2189
2190```sh
2191node /absolute/path/to/receipts/dist/cli.js run -- ./verify
2192printf 'Verification passed.\n' | node /absolute/path/to/receipts/dist/cli.js check --strict -
2193```
2194
2195The installed command uses absolute Node and CLI paths so it works from subdirectories. Keep that build at the same path, or reinstall after moving it. Hooks can be disabled or overridden by the host or user; this is not an unbypassable security boundary. Fake-agent end-to-end tests are local protocol tests, not evidence of live host activation.
2196
2197### Export the evidence
2198
2199Save a response in the ignored ledger directory, then render it:
2200
2201```sh
2202printf 'Verification passed.\n' > .receipts/message.md
2203node /absolute/path/to/receipts/dist/cli.js report --html .receipts/message.md > .receipts/report.html
2204```
2205
2206The single HTML file contains the message’s verdicts and ledger timeline. Follow a claim to the exact receipt and back. Expand code identity and redacted output tails using the keyboard. It works offline and without JavaScript, external font requests, accounts or a server. An unreadable or corrupt ledger produces an explicit error report and exit 2, never a reassuring timeline. --strict returns 1 for unsupported claims. The file is a snapshot, can be edited, and is not signed. Inspect it before sharing: paths and unrecognized secrets may remain.
2207
2208Reports use IBM Plex Sans for reading, Plex Mono for code and records, and Plex Sans Condensed for headings and labels. Eight Latin WOFF2 faces from Fontsource 5.3.0 are vendored under SIL OFL 1.1 in assets/fonts, embedded in each standalone export and preloaded for the three main faces. No font service is contacted at runtime. See the font licence inventory and the before/after layout checks.
2209
2210### Use the CLI directly
2211
2212The package exposes a receipts bin for eventual installation; this unpublished checkout uses node dist/cli.js. Publication remains disabled with private: true; the unscoped npm name is occupied. Add .receipts/ to the target repository’s .gitignore before use.
2213
2214```sh
2215node dist/cli.js --help
2216node dist/cli.js run --label tests -- npm test
2217printf 'Tests pass.\n' | node dist/cli.js check --strict -
2218node dist/cli.js verify
2219node dist/cli.js ls
2220```
2221
2222Human reports align verdicts, reasons and receipt IDs. Color communicates outcome and is enabled only on a TTY; NO_COLOR (even empty) disables it. Redirected output and JSON stay plain. Long text wraps to terminal width and control sequences are displayed rather than executed. run still streams the child’s output unchanged.
2223
2224annotate atomically rewrites Markdown with receipt references. Save drafts under .receipts/: writing or annotating a nonignored file changes the fingerprint and makes previous receipts stale.
2225
2226### Sign recorded evidence
2227
2228```sh
2229node dist/cli.js attest --subject artifact.json --output .receipts/artifact.dsse.json
2230node dist/cli.js attest --record .receipts/import.json --subject public/recording.json --output .receipts/import.dsse.json
2231node dist/cli.js verify .receipts/import.dsse.json --key .receipts/keys/ed25519-public.pem --subject-root .
2232```
2233
2234The first command selects the latest integrity-checked local ledger entry; --receipt UUID selects another. The import path signs supplied archival facts without rerunning anything. Both include original command metadata and SHA-256 subjects in a DSSE envelope. Incomplete archives use nulls and a checked missing-field disclosure; a display string is never parsed into invented argv or output digests. Known observation timestamps remain separate from execution times and signing time.
2235
2236receipts verify FILE --key ... checks signatures. Without a filename, receipts verify retains its ledger-integrity meaning. JSON reports signature validity, recorded exit success and subject-file checks separately. See the v3 delivery record for vectors, browser measurements and limits.
2237
2238### Commands
2239
2240Command · Behavior
2241| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
2242receipts run [--label NAME] -- COMMAND [ARG…] · Stream output unchanged; append evidence; preserve the command's exit code or signal.
2243receipts run --shell -- 'COMMAND STRING' · Explicit shell opt-in. Shell receipts are recorded but cannot verify claims.
2244receipts check [--strict] [--json] [FILE|-] · Extract assertions and show aligned verdicts, or a JSON report. Input defaults to stdin.
2245receipts attest --subject FILE [--record FILE] [--output FILE] · Sign a selected receipt or supplied import as a DSSE envelope; no command rerun.
2246receipts verify FILE --key PUBLIC.pem [--subject-root DIR] · Verify a pinned-key signature; optionally check subject files.
2247receipts verify [--json] [--checkpoint FILE] · Validate every receipt, its chain, and the local checkpoint; optionally require a separately retained checkpoint.
2248receipts ls [--json] · List receipts in ledger order.
2249receipts show ID [--json] · Show a receipt as JSON, using its full UUID.
2250receipts report --html [--strict] [FILE|-] · Export a self-contained evidence report; stdin by default.
2251receipts hook install --project DIR [--agent claude|codex|both] · Merge project-local Stop hooks; never changes user configuration or trust.
2252receipts hook run --project DIR · Host entry point: read direct Stop JSON on stdin and emit a decision.
2253receipts annotate FILE · Atomically rewrite Markdown with references and verdicts.
2254
2255check --strict and annotate exit 1 for unsupported claims. Operational errors—invalid input, corrupt evidence, Git or I/O failures—exit 2. Ordinary check reports verdicts without failing on unsupported claims. A message with no recognized claims exits zero and the human output says so; this is not evidence that the message is correct. A failed receipt write also exits 2, even if the wrapped command succeeded. Child exit codes can overlap these codes; consult the error message and ledger.
2256
2257### How it works
2258
22591. Record. run finds the Git root and fingerprints HEAD, the index, file modes, tracked working files and nonignored untracked contents. Staged and unstaged changes are distinct. An unborn repository works too. Paths and symlink targets are hashed without following symlinks. The index and raw contents represent both diffs directly, avoiding machine-specific Git diff formatting.
22602. Execute. It spawns an argv array, with no shell by default. Stdout and stderr stream through unchanged with backpressure. SHA-256 digests cover the exact original bytes. Only bounded, redacted tails and recognized scalar summaries are retained; full output is never saved.
22613. Bind. A second fingerprint catches code changes during execution. Each schema-validated receipt includes the preceding receipt's hash. An exclusive writer lock prevents a forked chain. The ledger and checkpoint are private local files in .receipts/.
22624. Check. A deterministic grammar extracts assertions. Literal command patterns choose the newest matching command, by start time with ledger order breaking ties. Command prefixes, or trusted labels for aggregate verification, select a kind; labels alone do not prove success. The same code fingerprint and a zero exit are required.
2263
2264The ledger is .receipts/ledger.jsonl; .receipts/checkpoint.json records its count and terminal hash. check, ls, show and annotate validate integrity before using any evidence. run refuses to execute when existing evidence is corrupt.
2265
2266#### Verdicts
2267
2268Verdict · Meaning
2269| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
2270VERIFIED · A matching command exited zero against the current fingerprint, without changing it. Numeric claims also agree with a recognized output summary.
2271STALE · It exited zero, but code changed since or during execution.
2272FAILED · The latest matching command exited nonzero or was terminated by a signal. An older success does not hide it.
2273MISMATCH · A claimed number differs from the parsed output.
2274UNBACKED · No matching command exists, or the numeric summary cannot be established.
2275VAGUE · Undefined verification scope; always requires human review and fails strict checking.
2276
2277VAGUE means an assertion such as “Everything is green” or “All green” names no definite checks. It always requires human review and fails --strict, even if every recorded command succeeded. It never carries a receipt reference. Replace it with specific, checkable assertions.
2278
2279Precedence is FAILED → STALE → numeric evidence → VERIFIED once a command is selected. A numerical mismatch on stale code is reported as STALE. Missing numerical evidence is UNBACKED. The checker does not search backward for a more flattering result.
2280
2281#### Claim grammar and summaries
2282
2283Defaults cover numerical test assertions (“All 218 tests pass”, “Every 12 tests are passing”), suite and runner assertions (“The test suite passes”, “npm test passes”), clean lint, passing typecheck, successful builds, percentage coverage, vulnerability counts (including zero), and deployment. “Lint and typecheck are clean” produces two independent claims, each anchored to its subject. A numerical coordinated subject retains its count. Unscoped green assertions receive VAGUE rather than disappearing. Aggregate check assertions use the separate verification kind described below.
2284
2285Quoted examples, code blocks, blockquotes, comments, negations and common hypothetical phrasing are excluded. Entire claims inside inline code are examples; a formatted subject followed by an assertion outside code, such as `npm test` passes, is checkable. Conditions before or after a claim and qualified exceptions are not unconditional successes. This remains a bounded grammar: other real claims can be missed, and a strict pass with zero recognized claims proves nothing.
2286
2287Explicit runner assertions also require that runner's command family: a successful pytest run cannot verify “npm test passes”. Known invocation aliases, such as npm run test and python3 -m pytest, are normalized. Generic “tests pass” still selects by verification kind.
2288
2289Numbers are parsed from Vitest, Jest, pytest, Cargo test and verbose Go test output. Cargo target summaries are summed; Go counts top-level --- PASS: lines from go test -v. Plain or cached Go summaries do not prove a test count. For Vitest, Jest and pytest, the final recognized summary wins; wrappers that concatenate independent runs need a custom integration. Coverage means the statements column in an All files table, pytest's TOTAL percentage, or an explicit Coverage: X% summary. It does not mean branch coverage. “No vulnerabilities” requires a recognized zero-vulnerability summary, not just an audit exit code.
2290
2291Discovery, help, dry-run, compile-only and known skip flags are excluded from command matching. This is deliberately conservative, but command names and configured patterns still rely on local trust: a script called test can do anything. Arbitrary tool versions and output formats are not automatically supported.
2292
2293#### Aggregate verification claims
2294
2295“Verification passed”, “All checks pass”, “Checks are green”, a standalone “Verified”, and “Everything passes” assert aggregate verification. They require a project verification receipt, rather than an individual test, lint or build receipt. Defaults recognize ./verify, npm run check, make check and npm run gate, plus equivalent pnpm/yarn/bun check and gate scripts. Named runner assertions such as “npm run check passes” also require that command family.
2296
2297Alternatively, a receipt can explicitly identify its command as project verification with a trusted label: verify, verification, check, checks, gate, ./verify, npm run check, make check or npm run gate. Labels are case-sensitive policy inputs. Review what the labeled command actually does; the checker cannot inspect its coverage. Configuration extends these commands and labels. A verification label never establishes an individual test, lint, typecheck or build claim, and cannot bypass shell, discovery or dry-run exclusions.
2298
2299```sh
2300node dist/cli.js run -- ./verify
2301printf 'Verification passed.\n' | node dist/cli.js check --strict -
2302```
2303
2304The latest matching receipt uses the same FAILED and STALE rules as other kinds. Missing evidence is UNBACKED. Numeric aggregate claims such as “3 checks passed” retain the count but remain UNBACKED because no aggregate check-count summary parser exists. “Everything is green” remains VAGUE and requires human review.
2305
2306#### Configuration
2307
2308Optional receipts.config.json in the Git root extends the defaults:
2309
2310```json
2311{
2312 "phrases": {
2313 "tests": ["QA is green"]
2314 },
2315 "commands": {
2316 "tests": [["node", "tools/qa.js"]],
2317 "typecheck": [["npm", "run", "check-types"]],
2318 "verification": [["node", "tools/verify.js"]]
2319 },
2320 "verificationLabels": ["project-validation"]
2321}
2322```
2323
2324Phrases are case-insensitive literals with word boundaries; command patterns are case-sensitive argv prefixes. Bare executable names match by basename; executable paths such as ./verify resolve against the receipt’s invocation directory and require a path invocation. verificationLabels extends the trusted, case-sensitive aggregate labels. These settings do not execute code or accept user-supplied regexes. Custom phrases express qualitative claims and extend the grammar without replacing overlapping built-in claims. Built-in numbers and VAGUE review requirements cannot be erased by a larger custom literal. Config is runtime-validated and limited to 64 KiB. Changing configuration changes the fingerprint. Review command patterns as verification policy.
2325
2326### Design decisions and trust
2327
2328- Evidence and bounded attestation. A receipt records what this local recorder observed. It cannot prove test quality, completeness, author identity, a trustworthy runner or honest output. The ledger remains unsigned; a forged ledger with a recomputed checkpoint can pass. Optional attest exports bind selected recorded facts and subject digests to a pinned signer key. They do not retroactively authenticate the original execution or automatically change check policy. Protect the producer and retain independent trust anchors.
2329- Truncation needs an anchor. The chain detects interior edits, deletion and reordering. The checkpoint also detects suffix removal, including deletion of the final complete line. An unterminated final line is rejected. Deleting both files is indistinguishable from having no receipts; a separately held checkpoint detects that too. Interrupted two-file writes fail closed and need investigation, not automatic repair.
2330- Code identity has a boundary. Git-ignored files, .receipts/, environment variables, external tools, network state and external services are outside the fingerprint. A before/after snapshot cannot detect a transient edit reverted during execution. Submodules and non-file entries are rejected instead of incompletely fingerprinted. No Git commit is required.
2331- Deployment stays bounded. VERIFIED for “deployed” means a configured deploy command exited zero against this code. It does not establish a live revision, health, traffic, authenticated behavior or human acceptance.
2332- Local, small and inspectable. One runtime dependency, Zod. No telemetry, server, credentials or model. See architecture and ledger format and the complete dependency licence inventory. The Vite 7 override keeps the development test toolchain within this project's permissive licence allowlist.
2333
2334### Privacy and operational limits
2335
2336.receipts/ is ignored in this repo. Add .receipts/ to the target repository's .gitignore before using the tool there. The fingerprint excludes the ledger directory regardless. Never wrap a command containing credentials on its command line if you can avoid it.
2337
2338Common tokens, API keys, bearer/basic credentials, JWTs, private keys and connection strings are redacted in stored argv, labels and tails. Redaction is best effort. Live output is unchanged; terminals and downstream tools can still retain secrets. Paths and arbitrary unrecognized secrets can remain in metadata. Do not upload a ledger without inspecting it. Raw output digests do not reconstruct output, but they can expose equality or permit guesses about low-entropy content.
2339
2340Tails retain at most 2,048 characters per stream. Oversized lines are omitted rather than keeping a potentially sensitive suffix. Summary lines are bounded to 8,192 characters; longer lines do not establish numeric evidence. Claim input is capped at 1 MiB; ledgers at 32 MiB. Archive a complete ledger and checkpoint together before starting a new one. A crash can leave .receipts/write.lock; confirm the writer has stopped before removing that lock. There is no automatic lock stealing or corruption recovery.
2341
2342Signals are forwarded to the command's process group on POSIX and to the child on Windows. Full signal semantics are POSIX-specific; local acceptance is on macOS, with Ubuntu configured in CI. Subprocesses execute with the caller's permissions. This tool is not a sandbox, a secret scanner or a replacement for code review.
2343
2344### Integrations
2345
2346The installed project hooks are the local stopping gate. Examples include a compatibility adapter to that same handler, an agent instruction snippet and an artifact-based GitHub Actions PR-body check. The hook follows the documented Stop protocol; its synthetic integration tests exercise the actual local CLI. The Actions example follows GitHub's artifact guidance, includes hidden evidence files explicitly, and keeps PR prose out of shell source. Both are opt-in examples; neither is enabled by the package.
2347
2348The handler rechecks continuations. Host-level interruption, continuation limits, startup failures and configuration can still allow stopping. Use an independently controlled CI check for enforcement. The Actions example is not a security boundary if the same untrusted contributor can change the checker, workflow and evidence producer. No hosted workflow execution is claimed by the local tests.
2349
2350### Evaluation: regression results and blind measurements
2351
2352The tuning corpus is implementation data. Its 100% is a regression result, not an estimate of how often arbitrary agent messages will be caught. Three other synthetic corpora were independently authored and hashed before their corresponding grammar changes. The implementer and reviewer did not inspect them until each implementation was frozen. Source hashes and the original results are retained.
2353
2354Evaluation · Messages scored · Precision · Recall · What it establishes
2355| ---------------------------------- | --------------- | --------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
2356Current tuning · 168 · 100% · 100% · Known examples pass after implementation and repairs.
2357Broad held-out v1, first blind run · 71 of 72 · 94.23% · 92.45% · First measurement of its frozen earlier grammar.
2358Broad held-out v2, first blind run · 81 of 84 · 95.24% · 93.75% · Different author and new messages, before later repairs.
2359Focused held-out, first blind run · 48 of 48 · 96.55% · 93.33% · Original requested phrase families; narrower than the broad sets.
2360
2361These are exact-span, kind and numeric-value measurements. A wrong span counts as both a false positive and a false negative. The broad runs each differed on five messages: two span differences, two unsupported forms, and one non-assertion misclassified as a result. The focused run differed on one coordinated phrase, “All 28 tests and the build passed”. The narrower focused score is not directly comparable with the broader scores. These are curated synthetic examples from a feature brief, not random samples of real agent language or production accuracy.
2362
2363Exact message overlap with the tuning and previously exposed sets was removed at each first measurement: one, three and zero messages respectively. The failures were then promoted into tuning and repaired. All three original files remain byte-for-byte frozen and now serve as regression data. The current grammar matches all 72, 84 and 48 messages under the explicit current classification policy: five former VAGUE targets are now verification claims. That versioned projection changes only those kinds, preserving original spans, values and historical gold for the archived measurements. None remains an untouched accuracy test for the final grammar. A new blind corpus is needed for another generalization estimate; a later 100% regression score must not replace the first blind score.
2364
2365The focused score is executable evidence: the frozen extractor exactly matches the pre-inspection source hashes. The evaluator compiles it, replays its original 28 true positives / 1 false positive / 2 false negatives, and requires that result to match the original report. The live extractor is tested separately and fixes the exposed case. Both older broad scores are retained recorded measurements, not replayed against the final grammar.
2366
2367Inspect the protocols, source hashes and first reports: broad v1, v1 report, v1 sources; broad v2, v2 report, v2 sources; focused, focused report, focused sources.
2368
2369The user-reported agent-race phrase “Verification passed” is retained separately in the reported regression set, with its supplied ./verify context and provenance. Its current result is 1 of 1 messages matched (100% precision and recall). This case was known before the fix: it is neither a blind measurement nor independently observed production evidence. No transcript or sibling repository was accessed.
2370
2371npm run eval prints currentRegressions separately from heldOutFirstPass. The former reruns current code and must have zero false positives and negatives on every corpus for CI to pass. The latter preserves earlier imperfect measurements and replays the frozen focused extractor. --set tuning checks current tuning only; --set regression checks all former held-out sets with current code; --set held-out validates the archives and replays the first focused score. Historical failures remain visible; they are not asserted to be current successes.
2372
2373The v2.1 typography review records the current report styling and monochrome print checks. The original v2 acceptance report records both visual critique passes, browser results, measured performance and remaining limits. The report ships zero JavaScript; this is a static evidence document with native controls.
2374
2375### Development and contributing
2376
2377```sh
2378npm ci
2379npm run typecheck
2380npm run lint
2381npm test
2382npm run eval
2383npm audit --audit-level=high
2384npm run licenses
2385npx playwright install chromium firefox webkit
2386npm run test:browser
2387```
2388
2389Those are the local checks; CI uses playwright install --with-deps on Ubuntu. Browser checks are part of npm run gate after browser installation. npm test builds the bin and runs Vitest unit, adversarial, filesystem and executable integration tests. Tests use synthetic data (plus the explicitly supplied regression phrase) and temporary repositories under ignored .tmp/; no sessions, accounts, remote services or Git commits are needed. npm run eval compiles the archived experiment fixture, checks current regression corpora and reports the recorded blind measurements separately. It fails on any current regression mismatch, changed frozen bytes or focused replay discrepancy. See the evaluation section above for provenance and limits.
2390
2391For contributions, include a minimal synthetic regression for any parser, verdict, fingerprint, redaction or subprocess behavior change. Add grammar examples and counterexamples to test/fixtures/claims.json; do not edit frozen corpora, snapshots or first reports to improve a metric. Collect and seal a new unseen set before a future grammar change. Keep trust boundaries runtime-validated and subprocess arguments out of shell source. Run the full gate, document changed limits and keep modules small. Report reproducible defects with synthetic messages and redacted receipts; never attach private transcripts or credentials.
2392
